title: Documented data store selection
statement: Each system SHOULD select its data store type from a documented assessment of access pattern, consistency need, scale, read and write ratio, and operational maturity.
applies_when: A new system or a new data store is proposed.
rationale: A store chosen by habit fits its workload poorly, and adding stores without need brings the premature fragmentation Azure warns about.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: The design record names the store type and addresses each of the five assessment factors.

title: Separate transactional and analytical workloads
statement: Analytical workloads SHOULD run on a store separate from the OLTP system of record.
applies_when: A system of record also serves reporting or analytics.
rationale: Analytical scans interfere with transactional load, and row and column storage are optimized for different work.
exceptions: A row store with a columnar replica (HTAP) is permitted for operational analytics. A read replica is permitted only where the reports do not feed decisions. Other deviations need a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: HTAP evidence supports claims about architecture, not named products: BENCH-14 anonymizes commercial systems and BENCH-13 is a vendor measuring its own product.
check_description: The architecture record shows where analytical queries run and, if they share or replicate the system of record, which permitted exception applies.

title: Engine enforcement of integrity in systems of record
statement: An OLTP system of record MUST declare in the database engine every integrity rule the engine can enforce.
applies_when: Transactional systems of record on engines that enforce the constraint type concerned, including ERP, financial and SaaS core tables.
rationale: Rules held only in application code are bypassed by other writers and can lose races, which leads to silent corruption.
exceptions: Application-only enforcement is permitted only under a documented infrastructure limit, such as sharding or shadow-table online schema change (conflict C-08). The framework exception approver approves each case.
engine_notes: Foreign keys are governed by INT-002. Analytical platforms are out of scope and are covered by ARC-004.
check_description: Each business invariant listed for the model is traced to an engine constraint, or to an approved infrastructure exception.

title: Record what analytical platforms enforce
statement: Each data warehouse or lakehouse platform in use MUST have a record of which constraint types it enforces, and a constraint it does not enforce MUST NOT be treated as a data guarantee.
applies_when: Any analytical platform on which constraints can be declared.
rationale: Declared keys that are only informational let duplicates and orphans through while appearing to prevent them.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Snowflake standard tables and Databricks enforce NOT NULL and CHECK only, with PK, FK and UNIQUE informational. Redshift enforces NOT NULL and treats PK, FK and UNIQUE as informational. For DQ-03, the per-adapter table could not be attributed reliably from the fetched text, so use it only for its explicit statements.
check_description: A per-platform enforcement record exists, and every declared but unenforced key has a substitute test (see DQA-004).

title: Strong consistency for coordinated invariants
statement: An OLTP system of record SHOULD use strong consistency, through a single writer or consensus, for invariants that require coordination.
applies_when: Invariants whose validity depends on concurrent writers. [INFERENCE] Uniqueness, balances and document numbering are such invariants.
rationale: Eventual consistency with later compensation can accept conflicting writes that break the invariant before anyone can correct them.
exceptions: Eventual consistency with compensation is permitted for invariants shown not to need coordination, with a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Conflict C-63 concerns how CAP is framed and is unresolved as theory, but practical guidance agrees. PACELC system classifications are not used.
check_description: The design lists invariants that need coordination and states how each is protected.

title: Single owner per schema
statement: Each OLTP database schema SHOULD be owned by exactly one bounded context.
applies_when: Systems divided into domains or modules, such as ERP modules.
rationale: Without one owner, changes are uncoordinated and models from different domains blur together.
exceptions: A small Shared Kernel changed only by consultation is permitted. Other deviations need a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Every schema has one recorded owning context, and shared schemas are recorded as Shared Kernel.

title: Storage boundary per service
statement: A service MAY start with private tables or a private schema and MAY move to its own server when throughput, storage type or deployment needs justify it.
applies_when: Service or modular designs where storage is divided by service.
rationale: Splitting servers early gives up cross-boundary ACID and joins for isolation that may not be needed.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: No quantitative threshold for separating servers exists in the sources.
evidence: research/data_modeling_approaches.md#18.9 Physical strength of the bounded context
check_description: Where a server split exists, the record states which of the three reasons applies.

title: Number of analytical layers
statement: An analytical platform MAY use one presentation layer for simple sources and MAY add integration or medallion layers where audit or multi-source reconciliation needs them.
applies_when: Designing warehouse or lakehouse layering.
rationale: Each hop adds latency and cost, while too few hops lose traceability for audited or multi-source data.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Medallion is a layering pattern, not a data model, and is not a requirement (conflict C-07).
check_description: The layer list states the purpose of each layer.

title: Analytical data ownership model
statement: Analytical data MAY be owned centrally, by domains as data products, or by a hybrid of the two.
applies_when: Deciding who owns analytical data.
rationale: Domain ownership adds integration cost and central ownership can become a bottleneck, so the fit depends on the organization.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Hybrid is what adopters converge on. Evidence is case studies, and ARCH-16 has an interest as the originator's then employer.
check_description: The governance record names the ownership model and an owner for each analytical dataset.

title: Portable SQL where it exists
statement: Designs SHOULD prefer standard SQL constructs over vendor dialect where the engines in use support them.
applies_when: The design may need to run on more than one engine.
rationale: Vendor-only constructs raise the cost of moving engines, although standard features were adopted slowly and engine capability can justify dialect.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: ISO/IEC 9075 text was not read, so no clause-level claim is made and feature support must be confirmed per engine.
check_description: Vendor-specific constructs in the design are identified and each has a stated reason.

title: Explicit cardinality and optionality
statement: Each relationship SHOULD have its cardinality and optionality stated before keys are assigned.
applies_when: Conceptual and logical modeling.
rationale: Assigning keys before relationships are understood leads to late rework.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Every relationship in the model shows cardinality and optionality.

title: One notation per model
statement: A model MAY use Chen, IDEF1X, crow's foot or UML notation, provided one notation is used consistently within that model.
applies_when: Producing entity relationship diagrams.
rationale: Mixed notation makes cardinality and optionality harder to read. No evidence favors one notation for outcomes, so the consistency requirement is a judgment.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: The IDEF1X federal mandate is reported withdrawn, and the withdrawal date rests on Wikipedia. The origin of crow's foot rests on two opened pages and the 1976 paper is unread, so it is not asserted.
check_description: Each diagram uses a single named notation.

title: Association table for many-to-many
statement: A many-to-many relationship in a relational store MUST be realized as an association table.
applies_when: Relational stores.
rationale: A foreign key alone cannot represent the relationship, and the usual workarounds cannot be constrained.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Non-relational stores are out of scope. Whether the join row needs its own identity is not settled by these sources (see ERD-004).
check_description: No many-to-many relationship in the logical model lacks an association table in the physical model.

title: Association table primary key
statement: An association table SHOULD use the composite of its two foreign keys as primary key unless the row is referenced elsewhere or has its own lifecycle.
applies_when: Association tables in relational OLTP stores.
rationale: An unneeded surrogate adds an index and can allow duplicate pairs unless a further constraint is added.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: DES-13 supports only a publisher-listed antipattern name. Distributed engines can add their own composite key requirements.
check_description: Association tables have a composite key of both foreign keys, or a recorded reason for a surrogate.

title: Identity of dependent entities
statement: A dependent entity SHOULD carry its parent key in its identity, either within the primary key or as a unique constraint on parent key and local key alongside a surrogate.
applies_when: Weak entities and identifying relationships, such as document lines under a document.
rationale: Without the parent in its identity, a child row can duplicate its local key within a parent.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: The parent key in the child primary key comes from Chen and IDEF1X. The surrogate plus unique form is [INFERENCE] for ORM-centric schemas.
check_description: Each dependent table has a key or unique constraint that includes the parent key.

title: No polymorphic reference columns
statement: A column SHOULD NOT reference several parent tables through a type and identifier pair.
applies_when: Modeling a reference that may point to more than one kind of parent.
rationale: No foreign key can be declared for the pair, so the reference cannot be enforced.
exceptions: A supertype table or one foreign key per target are the alternatives. Other deviations need a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: DES-13 supports only the publisher-listed name, and its remedies were not read. Rails ships this pattern, which shows real-world tolerance.
check_description: No table has a type and identifier column pair acting as a reference without an approved deviation.

title: References across bounded contexts
statement: A reference between bounded contexts in separate stores SHOULD be held as an identifier, while a reference between contexts within one database SHOULD keep its foreign key until the boundary is approved for physical separation.
applies_when: A reference crosses an aggregate or bounded context boundary.
rationale: Foreign keys across a boundary couple contexts, while bare identifiers lose engine integrity and can leave orphans.
exceptions: Shared Kernel tables may keep foreign keys. Other deviations need a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: No source states a ban on foreign keys across contexts. It is [INFERENCE], while modular monoliths retain cross-table ACID (ARCH-04). This rule limits INT-002 only where a boundary is approved for separation.
check_description: Each cross-context reference is recorded as identifier or foreign key, with the boundary status.

title: Reference tables for amended code lists
statement: A code list that is amended over time SHOULD be modeled as a reference table with effective dating and SHOULD NOT be embedded as literals.
applies_when: Codes such as ISO 4217 currency codes that change over time.
rationale: Literal lists need a schema change for each amendment and cannot show which codes were valid at a past date.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: ISO 4217 shows that such lists are amended. Using a table is [INFERENCE] and is not stated by that standard. Enum limits are engine-specific.
check_description: Amended code lists are held in reference tables with validity dates.

title: Discriminator on complete subtype clusters
statement: A complete subtype cluster MAY make its discriminator a required attribute, and a model that claims IDEF1X conformance adopts this as a condition of that claim.
applies_when: Subtype clusters. Binding only for models claiming IDEF1X conformance.
rationale: An optional discriminator on a complete cluster leaves it unclear which subtype a row belongs to.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: The standard is reported withdrawn.
check_description: Models claiming IDEF1X conformance have required discriminators on complete clusters.

title: Primary key on every base table
statement: Every OLTP system-of-record base table MUST declare a primary key.
applies_when: System-of-record base tables.
rationale: Without a declared identity, rows cannot be reliably addressed, and logical replication of updates and deletes fails.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: InnoDB creates a hidden key if none is declared. PostgreSQL requires a replica identity for logical replication of updates and deletes. Citus requires the distribution column in primary keys. The MANDATORY level is the matrix author's elevation from strong vendor wording, based on Codd and replication requirements.
check_description: No system-of-record base table lacks a declared primary key.

title: Enforced foreign keys on non-sharded OLTP
statement: Non-sharded OLTP systems of record MUST enforce references between tables with database foreign keys.
applies_when: Non-sharded relational systems of record.
rationale: Application-only checks are fallible and leave orphan rows.
exceptions: Infrastructure limits such as sharding or shadow-table online schema change permit omission under INT-003, approved by the framework exception approver. Boundaries approved for separation are governed by ERD-007.
engine_notes: Foreign keys are not supported on user-partitioned InnoDB tables. gh-ost does not support them. PlanetScale support is unsharded only. Citus requires the distribution column. Foreign key cost at scale is a judgment: no independent evidence at scale and no MySQL measurement exist.
check_description: Each referencing column on a non-sharded system has a foreign key or a recorded INT-003 exception.

title: Compensating controls where foreign keys are unavailable
statement: Where foreign keys cannot be enforced, the reference column SHOULD be kept and indexed, orphan rows SHOULD be audited on a schedule, and the risk SHOULD be recorded.
applies_when: An approved INT-002 exception applies, such as sharding or shadow-table online schema change.
rationale: Without these controls, orphans accumulate and go unnoticed.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Controls are drawn from PlanetScale's published mitigations. Risk acceptance is [INFERENCE]. Alibaba prohibits foreign keys in its MySQL guidelines, which is the opposing position in C-08.
check_description: Each exception has an indexed reference column, a scheduled orphan audit and a recorded risk acceptance.

title: Reference column matches its key
statement: A reference column SHOULD have the same data type and width as the key it references.
applies_when: Any reference column, whether or not a foreign key is declared.
rationale: A narrower reference fails once the key outgrows it, as in the Buildkite 32-bit incident.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: MySQL enforces matching size and sign for fixed-precision types. Other engines were not confirmed.
check_description: Reference columns match the type and width of the referenced key.

title: Explicit delete and update action per foreign key
statement: Each foreign key SHOULD declare its delete and update actions explicitly.
applies_when: Every foreign key.
rationale: Implicit defaults vary by engine, so behaviour can differ silently.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL defaults to NO ACTION, which can be deferred, and RESTRICT cannot. In MySQL/InnoDB, NO ACTION equals RESTRICT and SET DEFAULT is rejected. InnoDB cascades do not fire triggers. Cascades are hidden from binlog consumers.
check_description: Every foreign key has reviewed delete and update actions stated.

title: Default referential action
statement: A foreign key SHOULD use CASCADE only for strict composition, RESTRICT or NO ACTION for independent objects, and SET NULL only for optional relationships.
applies_when: Choosing the action for a foreign key.
rationale: Cascades can cause accidental mass deletion, while always restricting leaves cleanup to application code.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Sources disagree and none settles it (conflict C-09). This default is [INFERENCE], with the split also seen in the PostgreSQL entry. GitLab runs database-owned data on PostgreSQL, and PlanetScale and Alibaba come from sharded MySQL.
check_description: Each CASCADE is justified as composition, and each other action fits the stated relationship type.

title: Deferrable constraints
statement: A constraint MAY be deferrable when reference cycles or bulk insert order require it and the engine supports deferral.
applies_when: Cycles or bulk ordering. Check engine support first.
rationale: Immediate checks can block valid multi-row changes, while deferral reduces portability.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Re-check needed: text marked [WF] in the research was read only through a summarizing fetch and is not confirmed against the raw page. Supported on PostgreSQL for UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, foreign key and EXCLUDE. Oracle supports deferral, and such constraints cannot be altered in place. MySQL/InnoDB has no deferral. The SQL Server CREATE TABLE grammar shows no deferral syntax [WF], which is known only from absence.
check_description: Deferrable constraints have a recorded cycle or load-order reason and a supporting engine.

title: NOT NULL by default
statement: Columns SHOULD be NOT NULL unless absence has a documented meaning.
applies_when: Modeled tables. Raw landing layers that accept source data as received are excluded (conflict C-53).
rationale: Undefined NULLs bring three-valued logic and ambiguous meaning into queries.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Primary key columns are NOT NULL on every engine.
check_description: Each nullable column has a documented meaning for NULL.

title: CHECK paired with NOT NULL
statement: A column whose CHECK rule must always hold MUST also be NOT NULL.
applies_when: Engines enforcing CHECK, for rules that must hold for every row.
rationale: A CHECK passes when its expression is NULL, so a NULL value escapes the rule.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Confirmed for PostgreSQL and MySQL. Behaviour on SQL Server, Oracle and analytical platforms was not captured, and the pairing is safe regardless.
check_description: Columns under an always-true CHECK are NOT NULL, including for composite conditions.

title: State NULL treatment in uniqueness rules
statement: A uniqueness rule over a nullable column SHOULD state its intended NULL treatment and how each engine in use implements it.
applies_when: Unique constraints or indexes over nullable columns.
rationale: Engines differ, so a rule assumed to allow one NULL or many can behave otherwise after a move.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Re-check needed: text marked [WF] in the research was read only through a summarizing fetch and is not confirmed against the raw page. No portable default exists (conflict C-83). PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct by default, with an option to change this. MySQL permits many NULLs [WF]. SQL Server allows one NULL per column in a UNIQUE constraint [WF]. Oracle has a composite-specific rule [WF], from a page reporting Release 26. A SQL Server unique filtered index is [INFERENCE], not a documented example. Superseded by TYP-034 under OR-21.
check_description: Each unique rule on a nullable column records the intended NULL behaviour per engine.

title: No-overlap rules for periods
statement: A rule that periods must not overlap for one business key SHOULD be declared in the database where the engine supports it.
applies_when: Effective-dated data, such as rates or prices, on a supporting engine.
rationale: Overlapping periods make it ambiguous which row applied at a given time.
exceptions: On engines without support, cross-row enforcement under INT-012 is permitted.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL offers exclusion constraints and, from version 18, WITHOUT OVERLAPS. MySQL has no exclusion constraint. Support on other engines was not captured. SQL:2011 is known through its committee authors, and the ISO text was not read.
check_description: Effective-dated tables on supporting engines declare the no-overlap rule.

title: Cross-table integrity rules
statement: A rule that spans rows or tables MAY be enforced with a trigger or other engine mechanism because a CHECK cannot safely reference other rows.
applies_when: An invariant that a single-row constraint cannot express.
rationale: A CHECK that reads other rows gives unsafe results, and application-only logic is open to races.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: On PostgreSQL, the wiki says rules should not be used. On InnoDB, cascaded foreign key actions do not fire triggers.
check_description: Each cross-table invariant names its enforcement mechanism and known bypasses.

title: Default dimension rows over magic literals
statement: Warehouse dimensional models SHOULD represent missing references with explicit default dimension rows and SHOULD NOT use magic literal values.
applies_when: Dimensional fact and dimension tables.
rationale: Magic literals are aggregated or filtered as real values and so give wrong totals.
exceptions: A documented end-of-time value on a period column is a distinct case and must be declared.
engine_notes: Within Kimball-method models, default rows for fact foreign keys are mandatory by that method (RP-5). SQL Server temporal tables use 9999-12-31 for open rows. The home rule for fact foreign keys is RPT-006.
check_description: Fact references resolve to a real or default dimension row, and no undeclared literal stands in for unknown.

title: Test warehouse key uniqueness
statement: Declared logical keys on warehouse and lakehouse tables SHOULD be verified by uniqueness and not-null tests in the pipeline.
applies_when: Platforms where keys are not enforced.
rationale: Declaration alone does not prevent duplicate keys.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Key declarations do not enforce on Snowflake standard tables or Databricks. Pipeline MERGE keys are an alternative control. Superseded by DQA-004 under OR-22.
check_description: Each table with a logical key has passing uniqueness and not-null tests or an equivalent load control.

title: Warehouse foreign keys under controlled loads
statement: Warehouse foreign keys SHOULD be non-enforced with lookup validation in ETL-controlled loads, and SHOULD be declared as trusted by the optimizer only when the data is known to comply.
applies_when: Warehouse tables loaded through controlled pipelines.
rationale: An optimizer that trusts invalid keys can return wrong results, and full enforcement adds load cost.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Databricks defaults to NORELY. Redshift's planner assumes keys are valid and advises against declaring doubtful keys. Conflict C-03 is resolved by context.
check_description: Each trusted key has a passing compliance test, and loads validate references by lookup.

title: Natural or surrogate key
statement: An OLTP entity with a natural key MAY use a surrogate primary key with a unique constraint on the natural key, which is the accepted default.
applies_when: Choosing the primary key of an OLTP entity. Warehouse key type is separate (decision RP-6, conflict C-11).
rationale: Natural keys can change or be wide, while surrogate-only keys let duplicates of the real-world entity in.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: No source measures this for OLTP, so the default is a judgment. Celko's text was not read and is not relied on. The strongest published surrogate arguments are for warehouses.
check_description: Tables with a surrogate key and a known natural key also have a unique constraint on the natural key.

title: Do not reuse or fill key values
statement: Retired key values SHOULD NOT be reused and gaps in generated keys SHOULD NOT be filled.
applies_when: Generated keys. Legal numbering of documents is a separate topic.
rationale: Reused values can attach old references to new rows.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Supported only by a publisher-listed antipattern name in DES-13, so the rule stays provisional until the book is read.
check_description: No process renumbers keys or assigns retired values.

title: Separate logical and physical design
statement: Each data model SHOULD be developed as separate conceptual, logical and physical levels.
applies_when: Any new model or major model change.
rationale: Mixing logical meaning with engine representation ties users to access paths and raises the cost of later change.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: The physical level carries engine types, indexes, partitioning and controlled redundancy.
evidence: research/data_modeling_approaches.md#2. Foundations shared by all approaches
check_description: Design records exist for each level and the physical model traces back to the logical one.

title: Modeling start point by data paradigm
statement: OLTP models SHOULD begin from normalized entities on relational stores and from access patterns on key-value, document and key-distributed stores.
applies_when: Designing an operational store.
rationale: Applying one paradigm's method to the other loses either query flexibility or predictable performance.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Access-pattern modeling applies on DynamoDB, Cosmos DB and MongoDB, and to key design on Spanner. Conflicts C-01 and C-06 are resolved by paradigm and operability.
check_description: The design states the paradigm and shows entities or a list of access patterns accordingly.

title: Record physical departures from the logical model
statement: Every physical departure from the logical model SHOULD be documented with its reason and the dependency it introduces.
applies_when: The physical model stops short of the logical model, or adds redundancy.
rationale: Undocumented redundancy becomes invisible, so copies drift and no one knows what must stay consistent.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Each departure between logical and physical models has a recorded reason and a stated dependency.

title: Supertype and subtype mapping
statement: A subtype hierarchy MAY use class-table mapping when a subtype attribute must be required or a subtype takes part in a foreign key, and single-table mapping otherwise.
applies_when: A supertype and subtype relationship is being mapped to tables.
rationale: One table loses required-value enforcement on subtype columns, joined tables cost joins, and concrete tables lose foreign keys to the supertype.
exceptions: Concrete-table mapping is permitted where no shared foreign key target is needed. Other deviations need a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: No independent or engine-neutral benchmark exists, so this default is a judgment. Hibernate favours joined tables for constraints, and EF Core defaults to one table and warns on joined-table performance. Native exclusive-arc enforcement was not covered. On PostgreSQL, the community wiki advises against table inheritance for subtypes (single source).
check_description: Each hierarchy has a recorded mapping and reason, and required subtype attributes are enforced under the mapping chosen.

title: Hierarchy storage pattern
statement: A hierarchy MAY be stored as an adjacency list, a materialized path or an engine-native hierarchy type, provided the choice records the read and write pattern and how cycles are handled.
applies_when: The model contains parent and child trees, such as charts of accounts or organizational units.
rationale: Recursive queries loop on cycles unless these are detected, and each pattern trades query complexity against write cost.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Adjacency is foreign-key enforceable. PostgreSQL offers ltree for indexed path queries. SQL Server hierarchyid is reported faster for subtree queries and slower for moving non-leaf nodes, with no figures published, and it does not enforce relationships as a foreign key does. Closure table and nested set have no opened source and are not assessed here.
check_description: Each hierarchy records its pattern, the read and write reason, and its cycle handling.

title: Typed columns for core attributes
statement: Keys, monetary values and attributes used for filtering SHOULD be typed columns and SHOULD NOT be held in JSON documents or entity-attribute-value tables.
applies_when: Core business data. JSON remains available for sparse or externally defined attributes, such as tenant custom fields.
rationale: Values outside typed columns cannot take the normal constraints, and are harder to index and validate.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: DES-13 supports only the publisher-listed name of the entity-attribute-value antipattern. Its legitimate-use text was not read. Superseded by TYP-024 under OR-24.
check_description: No key, money or filter attribute appears only within a document or a generic attribute table.

title: Large binary object placement
statement: Large binary objects MAY be stored in the database or in an object store with a reference, chosen by size and lifecycle.
applies_when: The model stores files or other large objects.
rationale: Storing in the database affects row size, while external storage loses transactional integrity and shared backup scope.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: No fetched detail supports either option.
check_description: The design records the placement and the size and lifecycle reason.

title: Physical levers in analytical design
statement: Analytical physical designs SHOULD specify distribution, sort, partition and clustering keys where the platform offers them.
applies_when: Massively parallel and cloud warehouses.
rationale: On these platforms such keys take the place of B-trees, so leaving them unplanned raises scan and join cost.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: B-tree column-order guidance does not transfer to clustering keys (conflict C-29).
check_description: Each large analytical table has its chosen physical keys recorded, or a stated reason for none.

title: Mutable physical layout on lakehouse tables
statement: Lakehouse tables SHOULD use mutable clustering or hidden partitioning where the platform supports it.
applies_when: The platform offers liquid clustering, hidden partitions or an equivalent.
rationale: A fixed layout has to be rebuilt when query patterns change.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Documented on Databricks liquid clustering and Iceberg. Availability is platform-dependent.
check_description: Tables on supporting platforms use the mutable layout, or have a recorded reason for a fixed one.

title: Published interface over internal schema
statement: Consumers outside the owning system SHOULD read from a published interface and SHOULD NOT read the internal OLTP schema directly.
applies_when: Data is consumed outside the owning team.
rationale: Direct use of internal tables couples consumers to the model, so internal changes break them.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: External consumers are listed against a published interface, and none reads internal tables directly.

title: Atomic values in relational base tables
statement: Relational system-of-record base tables MUST NOT store repeating groups, delimited lists or numbered-column arrays.
applies_when: Relational system-of-record base tables. Analytical nested types, raw landing layers and document stores are out of scope.
rationale: Values inside a list cannot be constrained, joined or indexed individually.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Nested data is a documented design choice on BigQuery, and in document stores. Atomicity for lakehouse Silver and Gold layers is unresolved in the research and is not covered here.
check_description: No base-table column holds a delimited list, and no table has numbered columns for one repeating fact.

title: Third normal form as OLTP default
statement: OLTP base tables whose non-key fields are updated SHOULD be in third normal form.
applies_when: Relational system-of-record tables whose non-key fields are updated.
rationale: Without it, repeated facts drift on update, and facts cannot be stored or kept without an unrelated row.
exceptions: Stopping short is permitted where performance requirements justify it, as Kent allows, with a recorded reason (MOD-003) approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: BCNF is a matrix option, but its primary text was not read, so this rule does not require it.
check_description: Reviewers confirm that no non-key field depends on part of a key or on another non-key field, or that a recorded deviation exists.

title: Check higher normal forms for multivalued facts
statement: A table that holds two or more independent multivalued facts SHOULD be checked against fourth and fifth normal form.
applies_when: A table combines independent multivalued facts.
rationale: Combining such facts multiplies rows and makes blank fields ambiguous.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Based on Kent's exposition only. The primary papers were not read.
check_description: Tables with several multivalued facts have a recorded 4NF and 5NF review.

title: Conditions for denormalized read shapes
statement: An analytical or read-model structure MAY be denormalized when the workload is read-dominant, the redundancy has one controlled write path, and the dependency is documented.
applies_when: Read-dominant shapes fed by a controlled load. Not a licence for OLTP base tables (see NRM-005).
rationale: Unmanaged redundancy produces read shapes that disagree with their source.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: The three conditions are [INFERENCE] from Codd and Kent. No vendor page states them.
check_description: Each denormalized structure names its write path and source dependency.

title: Keep OLTP base tables normalized
statement: OLTP base tables SHOULD NOT be denormalized for read speed where a read model or columnar replica can serve the need.
applies_when: Read performance pressure on a system of record.
rationale: Redundant copies in base tables create inconsistency for writers, and read models contain that cost outside the write path.
exceptions: Denormalization is permitted with a measured need and a single maintaining path, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: SQL Server indexed views are permitted with a warned DML cost (conflict C-19). No source quantifies OLTP denormalization cost.
check_description: Any redundant column in a base table has a measured need and a named maintaining path.

title: Warehouse integration shape
statement: A warehouse MAY add a 3NF or Data Vault integration layer when it has many sources or an audit need, and MAY omit one for few stable sources.
applies_when: Choosing the warehouse integration layer. Cross-reference decision RP-2.
rationale: An integration layer adds load complexity, while omitting one leaves multi-source data unreconciled.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: No independent benchmark of Data Vault against star exists (conflict C-86), so the choice is a judgment. Superseded by RPT-002 under OR-23.
check_description: The warehouse design records whether an integration layer exists and why.

title: Star before snowflake
statement: Warehouse presentation layers SHOULD use a star schema rather than a snowflake unless there is a recorded clear reason.
applies_when: Dimensional presentation layers.
rationale: Snowflaked dimensions add joins for users and tools.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: BigQuery nested and repeated fields are a documented alternative for hierarchical one-to-many data (conflict C-05). Wide-table questions are outside this rule (decision RP-1, conflict C-84).
check_description: Snowflaked dimensions in presentation layers have a recorded reason.

title: Sixth normal form for volatile data
statement: A warehouse MAY use Anchor Modeling or similar 6NF structures for highly volatile, sparse and heavily historized data.
applies_when: Volatile, sparse, heavily historized attributes.
rationale: Table counts and reliance on optimizer support are high, so it suits specialist cases only.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Evidence is the authors' own paper. Primary 6NF texts were not read.
check_description: Use of 6NF structures has a recorded volatility and sparsity reason.

title: Embed or reference in document stores
statement: Document models SHOULD embed data read together within size limits and SHOULD reference high-cardinality, unbounded or independently existing data.
applies_when: Operational document stores only.
rationale: Unbounded arrays and bloated documents degrade reads and updates, and duplicated data is expensive to update.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: From MongoDB documentation. Conflict C-01 is resolved by paradigm. No source evaluates this for ERP or ledgers.
check_description: Embedded collections have a stated growth bound, and referenced data is identified.

title: One controlled path for redundant data
statement: Each redundant value SHOULD be maintained through one controlled mechanism, such as a generated column or a single ETL or refresh process.
applies_when: Any redundant or derived stored value.
rationale: Several writers of one derived value let copies diverge.
exceptions: Deviation with a recorded reason, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Each derived column names exactly one maintaining mechanism.

title: Convention is documented
statement: Each platform SHOULD have one documented naming convention that states its scope and its authority.
applies_when: always
rationale: Without a written convention and a named authority, reviewers have no basis for accepting or rejecting a name, and drift is invisible.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Confirm a convention document exists, names its owner and states which systems it covers.

title: Convention is applied consistently
statement: Every new object MUST follow the approved convention in this file, so that one platform has one style.
applies_when: always
rationale: Mixed styles force every consumer to look names up and make automated checks unreliable. The style itself has no outcome evidence; only consistency is required by every style source.
exceptions: Inherited or vendor-managed schemas, with an exception recorded and approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Lint all new or changed identifiers against the approved pattern table; report the share of objects that fail.

title: Vocabulary comes from the business context
statement: Names in a bounded context SHOULD use that context's agreed business vocabulary, recorded in its glossary.
applies_when: transactional domain models; analytical layers are covered by NAM-004
rationale: Names invented by engineers diverge from the language the business uses, and the same word comes to mean different things in the same model.
exceptions: Different contexts may legitimately use different terms for one concept; the context owner approves the glossary.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Sample table and column names and confirm each business term appears in the context glossary.

title: One name per attribute
statement: The same attribute SHOULD carry the same column name in every table where it appears.
applies_when: always, within one bounded context or one analytical layer
rationale: When one attribute has several names, joins and lineage must be worked out by hand and errors go unnoticed.
exceptions: Role-qualified references under NP-04, and raw landing objects covered by NAM-007.
engine_notes: Oracle is the only one of the five database engines with formal naming guidance; the reading is from the 19c edition (THIN-15).
check_description: Query the catalog for columns with the same domain or foreign key target but different names.

title: Dropped names are not reused
statement: A name that has been dropped SHOULD NOT be reused for an attribute with a different meaning.
applies_when: always; most important where table formats or downstream consumers track columns by name
rationale: A reused name silently attaches old history, grants or consumer logic to new data. No source states this for names; it is inferred from table-format rules on column identifiers.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Iceberg forbids reuse of column identifiers; that is a rule about identifiers, not names. Name-tracked systems carry the risk without that protection.
check_description: Compare each added name with the history of dropped names and flag matches for review.

title: Portable character set
statement: Identifiers MUST use only ASCII letters, digits and underscores, and MUST start with a letter.
applies_when: always, for names the platform creates
rationale: Other characters need quoting, behave differently per engine and break tooling. ASCII also makes one character equal one byte, which the length limit in NAM-010 depends on.
exceptions: Raw landing objects under NAM-007.
engine_notes: MySQL permits only BMP characters in identifiers. Databricks Hive metastore schema and table names are limited to alphanumeric ASCII and underscores. Oracle discourages dollar and number signs. SQL Server permanent objects must not begin with at or number signs.
check_description: Test every identifier against the allowed character set and first-character rule.

title: Raw landing keeps source names
statement: Raw landing objects MAY keep source-system names unchanged, provided the first conformed layer renames them to this convention.
applies_when: only in the raw layer of NP-23
rationale: Renaming at ingest breaks traceability to the source, while carrying source names further spreads unsafe identifiers. The exception is inferred from layer-based enforcement.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Delta column names cannot differ only by case, so a source with case-variant names needs handling at landing.
check_description: Confirm no object outside the raw layer fails the identifier rules.

title: No reliance on quoting
statement: Identifiers SHOULD be created and referenced unquoted, and SHOULD NOT depend on quoting or letter case to be distinct.
applies_when: always
rationale: Quoting makes a name case-sensitive on some engines, and the same name then fails when referenced without quotes. Two names differing only by case do not survive a move between engines.
exceptions: Raw landing objects under NAM-007.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL advises always or never quoting a given name. Oracle does not recommend quoted object names. MySQL column and index names are never case-sensitive. SQL Server case follows database collation. Databricks and Delta names are case-insensitive when referenced.
check_description: Flag quoted identifiers in migrations, and names in one namespace that differ only by case.

title: Fit within every target engine
statement: Every identifier MUST fit within the lowest identifier limit of the engines on which it will be deployed.
applies_when: always
rationale: Engines reject or misbehave beyond their limits. PostgreSQL truncates longer names rather than preserving them, so two long names can collide.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Limits are listed in the derivation table in this file. SQL Server local temporary tables are limited to 116 characters. A separate Databricks column-name limit was not confirmed. MongoDB limits namespaces (255 bytes, 235 sharded); its field-name length was not captured.
check_description: Compare each identifier's byte length with the lowest limit of its declared target engines.

title: Portable identifier ceiling
statement: Identifiers SHOULD NOT exceed the portable ceiling of 63 ASCII characters given in the derivation table.
applies_when: any system that may run on, or replicate to, more than one engine; deployments on a single engine may approve its limit instead
rationale: A ceiling set per engine makes later migration or replication fail on names that were legal when created. The 30-byte figure comes only from Oracle below COMPATIBLE 12.2 and is outdated as a universal ceiling.
exceptions: Single-engine estates may adopt that engine's limit, approved by the framework exception approver. An estate with Oracle below COMPATIBLE 12.2 must use 30.
engine_notes: 63 is PostgreSQL's default limit, in bytes. It is the lowest of the current engine limits and equals 63 characters only because NAM-006 restricts names to ASCII.
check_description: Fail any identifier longer than the approved ceiling.

title: Reserved words and prefixes
statement: Identifiers MUST NOT be a reserved word, or use a reserved prefix, of any target engine.
applies_when: always
rationale: Reserved names fail outright or force quoting, which NAM-008 discourages, and system prefixes can collide with engine objects.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Reserved prefixes: pg_ on PostgreSQL; SYS_ and ORA_ on Oracle. Nonquoted Oracle identifiers cannot be reserved words. Reserved-word lists differ per engine and version and are not reproduced in the research; a check must load each target engine's own list.
check_description: Compare identifiers with the union of the reserved-word and prefix lists for declared target engines.

title: Lowercase snake case
statement: Identifiers SHOULD be written in lowercase with words separated by single underscores.
applies_when: always
rationale: Unquoted case handling differs by engine, so mixed case does not round-trip. Vendors and style guides converge on lowercase for portability, from different causes.
exceptions: Raw landing objects under NAM-007.
engine_notes: Oracle and Snowflake store unquoted names in upper case, so a lowercase name appears upper case in their catalogs; do not quote to preserve it. MySQL table case depends on the file system and lower_case_table_names, fixed at initialization; lowercase names and the value 1 are advised for InnoDB portability.
check_description: Test written identifiers in migration and model source against the lowercase, single-underscore form.

title: Plural table names
statement: Tables and views SHOULD be named with a plural noun as in NP-01, and the choice SHOULD be uniform across a platform.
applies_when: always
rationale: No source reports an outcome difference, so this is a judgment and consistency is the real requirement. Plural was accepted because more table-level examples in the research use it.
exceptions: Framework-mapped tables may keep the framework's default if overriding it would be costly, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Primary sources split. Rails and GitLab examples are plural; dbt's style guide is plural though its own Kimball tutorial is singular; Alibaba forbids plurals; Django defaults and Prisma models are singular, while Prisma calls plural tables common. EF Core follows the DbSet name. Linters treat it as configurable.
check_description: Check table names for grammatical number using a configurable inflection rule.

title: Full words and an abbreviation register
statement: Names SHOULD use full words, and an abbreviation SHOULD be used only if it is listed in an approved abbreviation register.
applies_when: always
rationale: Private abbreviations make names ambiguous and undiscoverable. Length pressure on constraint names still needs a controlled way to shorten.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Sources conflict and the conflict (C-25) is settled for this framework by owner decision B31. Oracle asks for full, descriptive, pronounceable names and dbt for no abbreviations. MySQL's optimization page suggests short unprefixed column names under 18 characters.
check_description: Split identifiers into words and flag any word in neither the dictionary nor the register.

title: No type-indicating prefixes
statement: Names SHOULD NOT carry a prefix that only repeats the object type or data type.
applies_when: tables and columns; the warehouse prefixes in NP-29 and NP-30 and the constraint and index prefixes in NP-16 to NP-21 mark role and are excepted
rationale: Such prefixes add length without information and become false when the object changes kind.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Flag table names beginning with a table marker and columns beginning with a data-type marker.

title: Three-part registry names
statement: An object-class, property and representation-term name form MAY be used, and it is required only where a registry or regulator mandates it.
applies_when: metadata registries or regulated data element catalogs
rationale: The form makes names self-describing at the cost of length. Its only direct reading in the research is an informative annex of a 2004 committee draft, so it is not presented as required by the standard.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: The published 2005 and 2015 editions of ISO/IEC 11179-5 were not read beyond the 2015 abstract.
check_description: Where a registry applies, confirm registered names follow its rule set.

title: Primary key column name
statement: A single-column surrogate primary key SHOULD be named as in NP-02.
applies_when: tables with a single-column surrogate key
rationale: Named keys let a join column keep one name across tables and models. The cost is a conflict with ORM defaults.
exceptions: Framework-managed tables that use the framework's unqualified key name, approved by the framework exception approver. They must keep NP-03 for the columns that refer to them.
engine_notes: dbt and sqlstyle favour named keys. Rails and EF Core favour an unqualified key name. MySQL's optimization page favours short unprefixed names. In pooled or sharded tables the key is composite: it includes the tenant or distribution column under TEN-014 and SCL-006.
check_description: Check that the single-column primary key of each table matches the pattern.

title: Foreign key column name
statement: A foreign key column SHOULD be named as in NP-03, or as in NP-04 where a table holds more than one reference to the same parent or the role matters.
applies_when: foreign key relationships, including unenforced ones
rationale: A reference whose name differs from the parent key hides the relationship from readers and catalog tooling.
exceptions: Framework-managed tables, as in NAM-017.
engine_notes: Role qualification in NP-04 is this framework's proposal; the research does not state it.
check_description: Compare each foreign key column name with the parent key name and the pattern.

title: Identifier suffix means a real key
statement: The key suffix in NP-02 and NP-03 SHOULD be used only for columns that are real keys, and identifiers issued by third parties SHOULD use NP-05.
applies_when: always
rationale: A column that looks like a key but enforces nothing misleads both readers and tools that infer relationships.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: This is one organization's convention (GitLab), generalized here.
check_description: List columns carrying the key suffix with no primary, unique or foreign key, and review them.

title: Boolean column names
statement: Boolean columns SHOULD be named as in NP-06.
applies_when: boolean columns
rationale: A question-form name states which value means true; without it, readers must look the meaning up.
exceptions: Inherited schemas, under NAM-002.
engine_notes: On MySQL the name form carries the meaning that the integer type does not.
check_description: Check that columns of boolean type match the pattern and that pattern-matching columns have boolean type.

title: Instant and date column names
statement: Columns holding an instant SHOULD be named as in NP-07, and columns holding a calendar date as in NP-08.
applies_when: always; strongest in analytical layers
rationale: A consistent suffix tells readers whether a value is an instant or a date, which prevents time-zone and boundary errors.
exceptions: Inherited schemas, under NAM-002.
engine_notes: The instant suffix implies UTC only where TYP-012 is applied. Check the type as well as the name.
check_description: Check that instant-typed and date-typed columns match their patterns.

title: Status column names and values
statement: Lifecycle status columns SHOULD be named as in NP-11, and stored status codes SHOULD follow the rules of NAM-012.
applies_when: columns holding the state of a record or process
rationale: One undifferentiated status name cannot say whose lifecycle it tracks once a table has more than one. No source in the research states a status column convention; this is a proposal.
exceptions: Inherited schemas, under NAM-002.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL enum labels are limited to 63 bytes.
check_description: Check that columns registered as status match the pattern, and that stored codes are lowercase.

title: Explicit constraint and index names
statement: Constraints and indexes SHOULD be named explicitly using NP-16 to NP-21, and SHOULD NOT rely on engine-generated names.
applies_when: any constraint or index that a migration may later alter or drop, including informational constraints on analytical platforms
rationale: Generated names differ per environment, so a migration written against one environment fails on another. The migration impact is inferred.
exceptions: When a name would exceed the ceiling in NAM-010, shorten it using the register in NAM-014; never rely on engine truncation.
engine_notes: Unnamed constraints receive generated names on SQL Server and MySQL. The prefixes are GitLab's and bind inside GitLab only. EF Core and similar frameworks generate names by convention, which need an explicit override.
check_description: Flag constraints and indexes created without a name or with a name not matching the pattern table.

title: Schema names
statement: Application schemas SHOULD be named for a business domain as in NP-22, and SHOULD NOT be named for a team or a technology.
applies_when: transactional databases that use more than one schema
rationale: Team names and products change while domains are more stable, so renames are avoided. No source in the research states a schema naming rule; this is a proposal.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Oracle database names are limited to 8 bytes, which is a different object from a schema. Tenant schemas are decided in the tenancy standards.
check_description: Review schema names against the domain list.

title: Warehouse layer names
statement: Analytical layers SHOULD be named by the single approved vocabulary in NP-23 to NP-26, and SHOULD NOT mix vocabularies on one platform.
applies_when: platforms with more than one analytical layer
rationale: Mixed layer words hide which data has been conformed and which rules apply. The number of layers is a separate optional choice; this rule only names those that exist.
exceptions: A platform with existing medallion names may keep them, recording the mapping and with approval from the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Databricks and Fabric use bronze, silver and gold; dbt uses staging, intermediate and marts. Medallion is a recommended pattern and not a requirement (C-07). The mapping between the vocabularies is this framework's inference.
check_description: List schemas in the analytical platform and confirm each maps to one approved layer.

title: Snapshot objects kept apart
statement: History snapshots SHOULD be kept in their own schema as in NP-27.
applies_when: platforms using snapshot-based history capture
rationale: Snapshots cannot be rebuilt from current source state, so they need protection from refresh and cleanup jobs on rebuilt layers.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Single-vendor advice from dbt.
check_description: Confirm snapshot objects sit only in the snapshot schema.

title: Conformed and mart object names
statement: Staging objects SHOULD be named as in NP-28, and dimensional objects as in NP-29 and NP-30.
applies_when: conformed and dimensional layers
rationale: Source-qualified staging names stop two sources colliding, and a role marker tells consumers how a table may be joined. Only the dimension marker appears in the research; the others are proposals.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: dbt's Kimball tutorial uses a singular dimension name, which differs from the plural default in NAM-013.
check_description: Check mart and staging object names against the patterns.

title: Measure column names
statement: Monetary, minor-unit, currency and quantity columns SHOULD be named as in NP-12, NP-13, NP-14 and NP-15.
applies_when: columns holding money, currency codes or quantities
rationale: A column whose name does not reveal its unit gets mixed with one in another unit. Only the unit suffix for integer amounts appears in the research; the others are proposals.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Check that decimal or integer columns registered as measures match their patterns.

title: Money is exact
statement: Monetary values MUST be stored in an exact decimal type or in integer minor units, and MUST NOT be stored or calculated in binary floating point.
applies_when: always
rationale: Binary floating point cannot represent most decimal fractions, so totals fail to reconcile. A dbt style-guide example casts an amount to float; it conflicts with this rule and must not be copied (C-27).
exceptions: Raw landing may hold a value as delivered in text or semi-structured form under TYP-026, but not in a floating type.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL numeric; MySQL DECIMAL (up to 65 digits; default DECIMAL(10,0)); SQL Server decimal (precision 1 to 38); Oracle NUMBER with precision and scale, where excess scale rounds and excess precision errors; MongoDB Decimal128; Snowflake NUMBER, or DECFLOAT for ledgers and variable scale. Databricks money guidance was not captured.
check_description: Flag floating-type columns registered as money or matching the measure patterns; test pipelines for casts to float.

title: No proprietary money types
statement: Monetary columns SHOULD NOT use a proprietary money type.
applies_when: always
rationale: Proprietary types carry no currency, and can round on calculation or depend on locale settings on reload.
exceptions: Single-currency, whole-cent, add-and-subtract use on PostgreSQL, which the PostgreSQL wiki tolerates, with framework exception approver approval.
engine_notes: SQL Server money and smallmoney truncate in calculations and store no currency. PostgreSQL money depends on lc_monetary and stores no currency.
check_description: Flag columns of a proprietary money type.

title: Scale fits the currency
statement: The scale of a monetary column SHOULD cover the ISO 4217 minor unit of every currency it may hold, and SHOULD NOT assume two decimals.
applies_when: always
rationale: Minor units vary from 0 (JPY) through 2 (USD, EUR) and 3 (KWD, BHD) to 4 (CLF, UYW), and change by amendment, so hard-coded scales lose value or misstate it.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: The list used was dated 2026-09-17. The ISO standard page itself returned 403, so the edition is not verified; the SIX lists are the source.
check_description: Compare declared scales with the largest minor unit among the currencies permitted for the column.

title: Mixed-currency minimum scale
statement: Columns holding amounts in more than one currency SHOULD have a scale of at least 4.
applies_when: stored transaction amounts in multi-currency columns; does not apply to exchange rates, unit prices or intermediate results
rationale: A lower scale cannot hold CLF and UYW amounts. This is a low-confidence inference from those minor units and from SQL Server's four-place advice; no source states a figure.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL Server's four-place advice concerns its decimal type in calculations.
check_description: List multi-currency monetary columns with scale below 4.

title: Currency stored with the amount
statement: Each amount in a multi-currency context SHOULD be stored with its currency, as an ISO 4217 alphabetic code.
applies_when: any column set that can hold more than one currency
rationale: An amount without a currency cannot be interpreted or balanced by currency.
exceptions: Single-currency systems may state the currency once in metadata, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: ERP products hold transaction, entity and optional reporting amounts together; that requirement belongs to the financial controls standards.
check_description: Confirm each monetary column has a registered currency column or a documented fixed currency.

title: Currency reference data
statement: Currency codes and minor units SHOULD be held as effective-dated reference data loaded from the ISO 4217 lists.
applies_when: multi-currency systems
rationale: Codes retire and minor units change by amendment, for example BGN moving to List Three when Bulgaria adopted EUR, so a static list goes wrong and history must stay valid.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Reconcile the reference data with the latest SIX lists and confirm retired codes keep their end dates.

title: Integer minor units
statement: Integer minor units MAY be used for monetary values only as a marked exception to exact decimal, if the column name marks the unit as in NP-14 and the currency is known from the row or from metadata.
applies_when: where integer arithmetic is worth the conversion burden
rationale: Unmarked integer amounts are read as whole currency units. Exact decimal arithmetic is much slower than integer, so the option is legitimate, but no source gives numbers.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: MongoDB prefers its decimal type over a scale-factor method. PostgreSQL states numeric is much slower than integer arithmetic.
check_description: Confirm integer columns registered as money carry the unit marker and a resolvable currency.

title: Exact quantities
statement: Quantities that must add up or reconcile exactly SHOULD use an exact decimal or integer type.
applies_when: stock, measured and billed quantities; not scientific or sensor measures where approximate values are acceptable
rationale: Inexact types make stock and billing totals disagree with their sources.
exceptions: Measures where approximation is acceptable may use floating point, recorded in the data dictionary.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL advises numeric for exact quantities. Snowflake reserves FLOAT for cases where imprecise results are acceptable.
check_description: Flag floating-type columns registered as reconciling quantities.

title: Quantity carries its unit
statement: Quantities SHOULD be stored with a unit of measure, and the scale SHOULD be declared per unit in the design record.
applies_when: columns that can hold more than one unit, or whose unit is not fixed by the column's definition
rationale: A quantity without a unit cannot be compared or converted safely. The research states no scale or unit rule for quantities; this is an inference by analogy with currency.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Confirm each quantity column has a unit column or a documented fixed unit, and a declared scale.

title: Exchange rates are exact
statement: Stored exchange rates SHOULD use an exact decimal type that holds the full precision the rate source delivers; no value set for a framework-wide precision.
applies_when: any stored exchange rate; PROVISIONAL and no value set, because no source addresses rate representation
rationale: Rates feed converted amounts, so rounding in a floating type carries into posted figures. This extends the money rule by inference.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: A rate and its reciprocal may disagree after rounding, and products differ on storing inverses (C-77); this is left to the financial controls standards.
check_description: Flag floating-type columns registered as exchange rates.

title: Exchange rate precision is a recorded decision
statement: Each deployment SHOULD record the precision and scale of its exchange-rate columns as a design decision, SHOULD hold the full precision the rate source delivers, and SHOULD NOT round a delivered rate on capture; no value set for a framework-wide precision.
applies_when: any stored exchange rate; PROVISIONAL and no value set, because no vendor or standard-setter read states a precision
rationale: A rate column narrower than what the provider delivers loses value silently, but any figure in this framework would be invented, so decision A14 records no value set.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: No vendor page states a precision standard. D365's example display does not establish one.
check_description: Confirm the design record states the rate precision and that it covers the provider's delivered precision.

title: Instants are unambiguous relative to UTC
statement: An instant SHOULD be stored in a UTC-normalizing type where one fits the required range, or otherwise under a documented UTC convention.
applies_when: any column recording a point in time
rationale: A local timestamp with no zone cannot be placed on a timeline, so ordering and duration calculations break across zones and daylight changes.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL timestamptz stores UTC and drops the zone; timetz is advised against, and the wiki is stricter than the manual on plain timestamp (C-24). MySQL TIMESTAMP ends 2038-01-19, while DATETIME has no conversion and needs an application UTC convention. SQL Server: avoid datetime; no official choice between datetime2 in UTC and datetimeoffset; treat datetimeoffset as a fixed offset (C-88). [WF] The datetimeoffset daylight-saving behaviour (ENG-09) was read through a summarising fetch and needs a re-check against the page before use. Oracle WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE normalizes to the database zone. MongoDB BSON Date is UTC. Snowflake notes TZ types hurt pruning and advises keeping a non-TZ column for filtering.
check_description: Flag instant-named columns with a zone-less type that lack a documented UTC convention.

title: Calendar dates use a date type
statement: A value with no time-of-day meaning SHOULD be stored in a calendar date type and not as an instant.
applies_when: birth dates, accounting dates, due dates and similar
rationale: A date stored as an instant shifts by a day when read in another zone.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Oracle DATE includes time to the second, so a date-only rule on Oracle needs an added truncation check.
check_description: Flag date-named columns with an instant type, and on Oracle test for non-midnight values.

title: Local time retained where it has meaning
statement: Where a local wall-clock time or source zone has business meaning, it SHOULD be stored separately as in NP-09 and NP-10.
applies_when: when the local time or zone is itself part of the business fact; analytical use is not addressed by the research
rationale: UTC normalization discards the original zone. No source covers future-dated local events specifically.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL states the zone is not retained. Oracle TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE does preserve zone information.
check_description: Review requirements for local-time semantics and confirm a separate column exists where they apply.

title: Half-open time ranges
statement: Time ranges SHOULD be expressed as an inclusive start and an exclusive end, and range filters SHOULD NOT use BETWEEN on instants.
applies_when: stored periods and range predicates on instants
rationale: An inclusive upper bound double-counts or misses rows at the boundary.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL:2011 periods are closed-open as reported by committee authors; the clause text was not read. SQL Server temporal tables use a 9999-12-31 end for open rows.
check_description: Review range definitions and search query code for BETWEEN on instant columns.

title: ISO 8601 for interchange only
statement: Date-time values exchanged between systems as text SHOULD use ISO 8601, and ISO 8601 SHOULD NOT be treated as a storage type.
applies_when: interchange formats
rationale: Ambiguous text dates are misread on exchange, and text storage loses type checks.
exceptions: ISO 8601 excludes non-Gregorian calendars; such interchange is excepted, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Test interface payloads against the ISO 8601 profile.

title: Text sizing follows the engine
statement: Text columns SHOULD be sized under the target engine's annex, and any declared length SHOULD be recorded as either a business limit or a storage choice.
applies_when: transactional engines; analytical sizing is not addressed by the research
rationale: Invented limits cause production errors, yet engines differ on whether unbounded text is costless (C-21), so a single portable size rule would be wrong on some engine.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL: unbounded text with CHECK for real limits; no performance difference apart from padding. MySQL: bounded VARCHAR with the smallest suitable type, considering row format and index limits. SQL Server nvarchar(n) counts byte-pairs, not characters. Oracle: use VARCHAR2, not VARCHAR.
check_description: Review declared lengths against the design record's business limits and the engine annex.

title: Fixed-length codes validated by content
statement: Fixed-length codes SHOULD be validated by a content rule on length and character class, and not by reliance on a padded fixed-width type.
applies_when: codes such as ISO currency codes
rationale: A padded type changes comparison and does not check content. The content rule is universal; the storage type is engine-specific.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: The research suggested a three-character fixed type or text with CHECK; the PostgreSQL wiki says not to use char(n) even for fixed-length identifiers. Resolve per engine.
check_description: Confirm registered code columns have a content rule.

title: Unicode-capable encoding
statement: A database SHOULD use one Unicode-capable encoding for text.
applies_when: always
rationale: Mixed or partial encodings lose characters and break comparison across columns.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: MySQL: use utf8mb4, since utf8mb3 is deprecated and expected to be removed. This specific name has single-engine evidence.
check_description: Query the catalog for database, table and column encodings.

title: Joined columns match
statement: Columns that are joined or related by a foreign key SHOULD have the same data type, width, character set and collation.
applies_when: foreign keys and recurring join columns
rationale: Mismatches cause implicit conversion, lost index use, and overflow where a referencing integer is narrower than its parent.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: MySQL says joined columns should share character set and type. Snowflake says never to use collation on join keys.
check_description: Compare type, width, character set and collation across each foreign key and registered join.

title: Native boolean
statement: Yes-or-no attributes SHOULD use the engine's native boolean type where one exists.
applies_when: transactional engines with a native type
rationale: Coded substitutes admit more values than true and false unless separately constrained.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: MySQL: use tinyint with the naming pattern in NP-06, per Alibaba. The research has no source for calling single-character flags an antipattern, and none is claimed.
check_description: Flag NP-06 columns that do not have the native boolean type on engines offering one.

title: Enumerated value sets
statement: A value set that can change or carries attributes SHOULD be a reference table referenced by a foreign key.
applies_when: transactional schemas; analytical layers use conformed dimensions instead
rationale: Native enums are hard to change, and a CHECK list needs a schema change for each new value. The reference-table default is inferred from engine limits; sources disagree, so a CHECK may serve small stable sets.
exceptions: A CHECK on text may be used for small stable sets, approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL enums cannot have values removed without re-creating the type. MySQL ENUM values are stored as indexes, sort by index, and invalid input in non-strict mode becomes an empty string.
check_description: Flag native enum columns and long CHECK lists for review against the approved option.

title: Native enums only for static sets
statement: A native enumeration type MAY be used only for a value set that will not change.
applies_when: truly static value sets
rationale: A static set avoids a join and a reference table, but a set that later changes becomes costly to alter.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: [WF] MySQL's online DDL matrix lists ENUM changes; it was read through a summarising fetch and needs a re-check against the page before use.
check_description: Review each native enum for evidence that the set is static.

title: JSON use is bounded
statement: Keys, money and attributes that are filtered or aggregated SHOULD remain typed relational columns and SHOULD NOT be held in entity-attribute-value tables, and JSON SHOULD hold only sparse or externally defined attributes.
applies_when: transactional schemas; lakehouse raw capture is TYP-026
rationale: JSON columns weaken constraints and indexing, and updates can rewrite or lock whole documents.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL advises small, atomic documents because any update locks the whole row. MySQL cannot index JSON directly and needs generated columns or multi-valued indexes; PostgreSQL uses GIN.
check_description: Review JSON columns and generic attribute tables for embedded keys, money or fields used in filters.

title: Native JSON type
statement: JSON documents SHOULD be stored in the engine's native JSON type where one exists.
applies_when: engines with a native type
rationale: Plain text gives no validation and no path access.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL prefers jsonb. Oracle says to use its JSON type for JSON columns. Snowflake and Databricks use VARIANT. SQL:2023 added a JSON type per secondary sources, so portability is engine-dependent.
check_description: Flag text columns registered as JSON on engines with a native type.

title: Semi-structured raw capture
statement: Raw landing layers MAY store source payloads in semi-structured or string form, provided typed columns are applied from the first conformed layer.
applies_when: raw landing layers; never serving layers
rationale: Typing at ingest can lose unparsed data, while carrying semi-structured data further loses the type guarantees downstream.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Databricks describes bronze as mostly string, VARIANT or binary. Snowflake advises flattening dates, numbers in strings and arrays. Delta enforces schema by default.
check_description: Confirm conformed tables have no semi-structured columns for fields declared in the contract.

title: Decimals declared at analytical landing
statement: Pipelines that infer schemas SHOULD declare decimal columns explicitly and not rely on inference.
applies_when: file or stream ingestion with schema inference
rationale: Inference can silently produce a floating type, which breaks TYP-001.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Spark inference defaults floats to double unless configured.
check_description: Compare inferred output types with the contract's declared decimals.

title: Numeric-looking identifiers are strings
statement: Codes and identifiers that look numeric but are not quantities SHOULD be stored as strings.
applies_when: codes with possible leading zeros or no arithmetic meaning
rationale: Numeric storage strips leading zeros: ISO 4217 numeric code 048 shows this directly. Phone, postal and national identifiers are inference.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Review numeric columns whose names suggest codes.

title: Width of generated integer keys
statement: Generated integer keys SHOULD be 64-bit, unless the table is a bounded lookup table.
applies_when: tables keyed by a generated integer
