applies_when: Personal data within GDPR territorial and material scope, or systems claiming ASVS 5.0.0 V14 conformity at L2 or above
rationale: ASVS requires identification and classification, and GDPR Art. 30 requires processing records. This rule requires legal review.
exceptions: The Art. 30(5) small-enterprise exemption is narrow, and is lost where processing is not occasional; do not rely on it without counsel.
engine_notes: Art. 30 requires records of processing and does not itself prescribe column-level classification.
check_description: The inventory covers all attributes in in-scope stores.

title: Data minimization under GDPR
statement: Systems holding personal data under GDPR MUST collect only the attributes necessary for a documented purpose.
applies_when: Personal data within GDPR scope
rationale: Art. 5(1)(c) and Art. 25 require minimisation and data protection by design. This rule requires legal review.
exceptions: Scope and necessity determined by counsel.
engine_notes: Each collected attribute needs a purpose (inference). Retention is covered by the retention and erasure group.
check_description: Each personal data attribute has a recorded purpose.

title: Encryption layer by threat
statement: A system MAY use volume or transparent encryption, column or application encryption, or client-side encryption according to its threat model.
applies_when: Where a threat model covers the data
rationale: No layer answers every threat: at-rest encryption addresses stolen media, not authorized sessions, and stronger layers remove query capability.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Always Encrypted imposes collation and type restrictions (SEC-23). Oracle column encryption restricts index range scans (MSOM-13). TDE backup files are encrypted with the DEK, and losing certificates loses data (SEC-24).
check_description: The chosen layer for each protected store is recorded against its threat.

title: Encryption decisions name their threat
statement: Each encryption decision SHOULD record the threats it addresses and those it does not.
applies_when: Whenever encryption is claimed as a control
rationale: Compliance claims from at-rest encryption alone overstate protection.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Each encryption record lists addressed and unaddressed threats.

title: Encrypted connections
statement: Database connections SHOULD use TLS with certificate verification.
applies_when: always
rationale: At-rest encryption does not protect data in transit.
exceptions: Local connections on a single host with no network path; approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Connections are confirmed to use verified TLS.

title: Stored PAN rendered unreadable
statement: Stored PAN MUST be rendered unreadable by one of the approaches listed in PCI DSS 3.5.1, and disk-level or partition-level encryption alone MUST NOT be relied on.
applies_when: Systems storing PAN within PCI DSS scope (a contractual industry standard)
rationale: Wording is from PCI DSS v4.0 SAQ D, not re-verified against v4.0.1. Requires legal review, and scope questions go to the organization's PCI assessor.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: The PCI text does not name TDE. Where file-level TDE falls is unresolved; ask the assessor. Listed approaches are one-way hashes of the entire PAN, truncation, index tokens, or strong cryptography with key management. Hashed and truncated forms of one PAN need correlation controls.
check_description: Each stored PAN column maps to a listed approach, confirmed by the assessor.

title: ePHI encryption
statement: Systems holding ePHI SHOULD encrypt it as if encryption were required.
applies_when: ePHI under HIPAA in the United States
rationale: Encryption is addressable today and a 2025 NPRM proposes making it required; final-rule status is unverified. This rule requires legal review.
exceptions: An addressable specification allows a documented equivalent and reasoning, confirmed by counsel.
engine_notes: The design-as-if-required position is an inference.
check_description: ePHI stores are encrypted, or an equivalent and reasoning are documented.

title: Masking is not a boundary
statement: Dynamic masking or redaction MUST NOT be relied on as the sole control for sensitive data.
applies_when: always
rationale: SQL Server and Oracle both document inference attacks using predicates against masked values.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL Server masking cannot be combined with Always Encrypted, does not stop updates, and high-privilege users can view originals (SEC-25). Oracle redacted values can be written back by updating applications (MSOM-13).
check_description: Each masked column has an additional control recorded.

title: Key handling
statement: Encryption keys SHOULD be held apart from the data, under a managed lifecycle, using authenticated encryption modes.
applies_when: Encryption is used, outside SEC-019
rationale: Keys stored with data fall with one foothold, and unmanaged keys cannot be rotated on compromise.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Tagging ciphertext with a key identifier allows multiple live keys (SEC-04). Separate key classes for recoverable and destruction-capable data are an inference.
check_description: Key storage, rotation triggers and cipher modes are documented.

title: Key handling for NIST-aligned systems
statement: US federal systems and systems claiming NIST alignment MUST hold keys apart from the data under a managed lifecycle.
applies_when: US federal systems, or systems claiming alignment with NIST SP 800-53 and SP 800-57
rationale: NIST SC-12 sets key management requirements for these systems.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SP 800-53 Release 5.2.0 changes were not reviewed.
check_description: Key management records match the stated controls.

title: Non-production data
statement: Non-production environments SHOULD use masked or synthetic data instead of copies of production.
applies_when: always. See SEC-021 and SEC-022 for stricter conditions.
rationale: Production copies in test expose real data under weaker controls.
exceptions: Where production data is needed, the copy must be protected at the production level; approved by the data owner.
engine_notes: SP 800-122 requires PII in test to be protected at the production level.
check_description: Non-production data sources are confirmed masked or synthetic.

title: No live PAN in pre-production
statement: Live PANs MUST NOT be used in pre-production environments unless those environments are in the cardholder data environment and protected accordingly.
applies_when: Systems within PCI DSS scope (a contractual industry standard)
rationale: Wording is from PCI DSS v4.0 SAQ D, not re-verified against v4.0.1. Requires legal review, and scope questions go to the organization's PCI assessor.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: 6.5.6 numbering is v4.0 and was not re-verified for v4.0.1.
check_description: Pre-production stores are confirmed to hold no live PAN.

title: PII in testing for federal systems
statement: US federal systems MUST limit personally identifiable information used for testing, training and research.
applies_when: US federal systems under NIST SP 800-53 PM-25
rationale: PM-25 limits this use of PII to reduce exposure.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Test datasets are reviewed for PII.

title: Hardening baseline
statement: A system MAY adopt a version-pinned CIS Benchmark for each engine major version as its hardening baseline.
applies_when: Where a hardening baseline is wanted
rationale: Unpinned hardening drifts as engines change. Benchmark PDFs are gated, so no specific recommendation is asserted here.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Benchmarks exist per engine major version; pin the benchmark beside the engine version.
check_description: The benchmark and version in use are recorded per engine.

title: Central policy on analytical platforms
statement: Analytical platforms SHOULD apply central, machine-enforced tag or policy controls instead of per-object grants for sensitive data.
applies_when: Analytical platforms holding sensitive data. Not applied to OLTP.
rationale: Per-object grants fall out of step as data is copied, and classification has to follow the data.
exceptions: Platforms without tag or policy controls; approved by the data owner.
engine_notes: Snowflake binds masking policies to tags and propagates them; Unity Catalog offers governed tags, row filters and column masks; BigQuery enforces policy tags. Policy type matching carries a risk. Other platforms' propagation was not examined.
check_description: Sensitive columns carry a tag or policy with an enforced control.

title: PII in dedicated structures
statement: An OLTP design MAY hold PII in dedicated structures linked by a surrogate.
applies_when: OLTP systems with PII, where pseudonymisation or encryption scope benefits
rationale: Separation narrows encryption and access scope, at a cost in joins.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Same-database placement may not achieve separation against all pseudonymisation domains.
check_description: Where used, the design records which attributes are separated and why.

title: Pseudonym maps held apart
statement: Where pseudonymisation is relied on under GDPR, the additional identifying information MUST be held separately from the pseudonymised data under separate access.
applies_when: Personal data under GDPR where pseudonymisation is relied on
rationale: Art. 4(5) requires separately kept additional information under safeguards. Pseudonymised data remains personal data. This rule requires legal review.
exceptions: Counsel determines reliance.
engine_notes: EDPB 01/2025 (SEC-16) is a consultation version. Tokenization vault designs were not researched.
check_description: The location and access of pseudonym maps are confirmed separate.

title: Passwords hashed
statement: Stored passwords MUST be hashed with a password-hashing algorithm and MUST NOT be reversibly encrypted.
applies_when: Systems storing passwords
rationale: Reversible storage exposes every credential if the key or data leaks.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Password storage is confirmed to use a password-hashing algorithm.

title: Masked output is not de-identified
statement: Masked output SHOULD NOT be treated as de-identified data without a de-identification assessment.
applies_when: Masked data shared or used for analysis
rationale: Not all masking tools provide what de-identification requires, so re-identification risk remains.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Datasets described as de-identified have an assessment on record.

title: No personal data in tags
statement: Tag values and metadata SHOULD NOT contain personal data.
applies_when: Analytical platforms using tags or metadata
rationale: Databricks warns that tag data is stored as plain text and may be replicated.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Stated by Databricks; other platforms were not examined.
check_description: Tag values are scanned for personal data.

title: Restricted access to security-critical tables
statement: Security-critical tables MAY be exposed only through views or column and row permissions.
applies_when: Security-critical applications
rationale: Direct table access exposes columns that callers do not need.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: MySQL column privileges exist [WF]; re-check before relying on them. Row-level capability was not found in pages read (ENG-06).
check_description: Direct table grants on security-critical tables are limited to the views or permissions recorded.

title: Tenant isolation required
statement: A multi-tenant system MUST isolate each tenant's data by a named, documented mechanism.
applies_when: Multi-tenant SaaS operational systems
rationale: A breach of the tenant boundary is treated by AWS as a potentially unrecoverable event for a SaaS business. The mechanism is a choice; isolation is not.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Mechanism differs per engine; see TEN-009 and TEN-010. AWS and Azure frame this requirement; the notes hold no equivalent Google page.
check_description: Design record names the isolation mechanism for every tenant data store.

title: No unintended cross-tenant results
statement: A query path MUST NOT return data from more than one tenant unless it is explicitly designed and approved to do so.
applies_when: Multi-tenant SaaS operational systems
rationale: Application filtering makes every query a potential leak, since one missing predicate exposes another tenant's data.
exceptions: Cross-tenant platform administration or reporting paths, approved by the data owner and listed in the design record.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Tests run the same request under two tenants and confirm no row from the other tenant is returned on each access path.

title: Tenancy model chosen deliberately
statement: Each multi-tenant system SHOULD record its tenancy model and the reasons for it before first production release.
applies_when: Multi-tenant SaaS operational systems
rationale: Changing the tenancy model later can be costly.
exceptions: Prototype systems holding no customer data; approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: none
check_description: A design record states the model, the tenant-count and compliance assumptions and the alternatives rejected.

title: ASTRA tenancy model
statement: ASTRA MUST operate as a shared pool with a tenant identifier on every tenant table, using dedicated databases only for tenants that meet a written silo trigger.
applies_when: ASTRA only, in its multi-tenant deployments. Other systems follow TEN-003. Deployments serving Saudi Arabia are outside this active decision: that part stays provisional until counsel confirms whether in-Kingdom retention (RET-018) forces a silo.
rationale: Without one approved model, key shape, restore, migration and security design diverge, and later change can be costly. The research has no ASTRA tenant counts or regulatory profile, so the default is a judgment and not a finding.
exceptions: Saudi deployments: the tenancy model requires legal review by counsel before adoption; see RET-018. Any other deviation needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Model choice is engine-neutral. Tenant-held keys are hard in a pool and harder when sharded (CLOUD-18).
check_description: ASTRA design records show the shared pool with tenant identifiers, each dedicated database names its trigger under TEN-005, and any Saudi deployment carries counsel's recorded position.

title: Silo triggers
statement: A tenant MAY be placed on dedicated resources when it needs its own keys, backup policy, data residency or regulatory separation.
applies_when: Multi-tenant systems where a tenant has one of the named needs. Whether a residency or sector rule applies is a legal question.
rationale: Pool placement makes per-tenant keys and restores difficult. Silo placement raises cost per tenant.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Each dedicated placement records which trigger applied.

title: Tenant identifier on pooled data
statement: Every tenant-scoped table in a pooled or sharded database MUST carry a non-null tenant identifier.
applies_when: Pooled or sharded multi-tenant data
rationale: Without the identifier, no predicate, policy or shard route can scope rows to a tenant.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Salesforce applies the equivalent as OrgID on shared generic tables (TEN-07).
check_description: Every table marked tenant-scoped has a required tenant identifier.

title: Tenant identifier in dedicated databases
statement: A hybrid or bridge deployment SHOULD keep the tenant identifier on tenant-scoped tables in dedicated databases as well.
applies_when: Hybrid or bridge deployments where tenants can move between pooled and dedicated placement
rationale: Tenants cannot be moved between placements without rewriting data if dedicated databases omit the identifier.
exceptions: Deployments that never move tenants between placements; approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Tenant-scoped tables in dedicated databases carry the same identifier as pooled tables.

title: Tenant context reaches the data layer
statement: Every request SHOULD carry verified tenant context to the data layer and be rejected if the context is absent.
applies_when: Multi-tenant systems
rationale: A request with no tenant context either fails unpredictably or runs unscoped.
exceptions: Approved platform-level paths under TEN-002.
engine_notes: SQL Server documents read-only SESSION_CONTEXT set after connecting (MSOM-05). The common PostgreSQL session-setting approach is not in the official page read.
check_description: Requests without tenant context are rejected on each access path.

title: Isolation enforcement point
statement: A pooled system MAY enforce tenant isolation through engine row-level security, application predicates or separate credentials; the accepted default is application predicates plus engine row-level security wherever the engine offers it and tenant identity can reach every query.
applies_when: Pooled multi-tenant systems
rationale: Sources disagree: PostgreSQL and Azure SQL present row-level security as the mechanism, while the Azure Architecture Center says many solutions avoid it. No independent performance measurement exists, so the default is a judgment.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Row-level security availability differs per engine. MySQL: no row-level feature was found in pages read; [WF] re-check before use, and treat this as absence of evidence only. BENCH-07 is one small practitioner test and is not relied on. SQL Server advises keeping policy objects in a separate schema and avoiding conversions, recursion and excessive joins in predicates (MSOM-05).
check_description: The design record names the enforcement point and, where it differs from the accepted default, the recorded reason.

title: Row-level security bypass set named
statement: Where engine row-level security is an isolation control, the design MUST list every principal that can bypass or alter the policy and MUST ensure the application runtime role is not one of them.
applies_when: Engine row-level security is relied on for isolation
rationale: Each engine leaves privileged principals outside the policy, so an unlisted bypass silently voids the isolation guarantee.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL: superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass, and owners do unless forced. SQL Server: policies apply to dbo, but dbo can alter them. Oracle VPD: SYS and default DBA roles are not bound; Oracle recommends Real Application Security for new work.
check_description: Compare roles holding bypass or policy-alter rights with the listed set, and confirm the runtime role is absent.

title: Isolation tested with the runtime role
statement: Row-level isolation SHOULD be tested using non-privileged roles, with table-owner bypass disabled where the engine allows.
applies_when: Engine row-level security is used
rationale: Tests run as an owner or superuser pass even when the policy is ineffective.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY binds owners. Enabling row security with no policy is default-deny. Equivalent controls on other engines were not researched.
check_description: Isolation tests execute under the application runtime role and fail if another tenant's row is returned.

title: Derived stores in isolation scope
statement: Where row-level security is the isolation control, each history table, change-capture feed and analytical copy of an isolated table MUST carry an equivalent tenant restriction.
applies_when: Row-level security is the isolation control
rationale: Row-level policies do not follow data into derived stores, and SQL Server documents whole-row leakage through change data capture.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL Server: Change Data Capture can leak whole rows, Change Tracking leaks primary keys, and temporal history tables need their own predicate. Other engines were not researched for this behaviour. Streaming tenancy was not researched.
check_description: Each derived store of an isolated table is listed with its tenant restriction.

title: Tenant-scoped uniqueness
statement: Unique constraints on tenant-scoped pooled tables SHOULD include the tenant identifier.
applies_when: Pooled multi-tenant data
rationale: A global unique constraint lets one tenant infer another tenant's values from conflict errors.
exceptions: Values that are genuinely global across tenants; approved by the data owner.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL referential-integrity checks bypass row security and can create covert channels (PGMY-07). SQL Server documents error-based inference (MSOM-05).
check_description: Unique constraints on tenant-scoped tables include the tenant identifier or have a recorded exception.

title: Tenant identifier in keys
statement: Pooled and sharded tenant-scoped tables SHOULD include the tenant identifier in the primary key, as its leading element where the table is sharded.
applies_when: Pooled or sharded multi-tenant data
rationale: Keys without the tenant identifier block co-location and tenant moves between shards.
exceptions: Single-tenant databases.
engine_notes: Citus requires it in every primary and foreign key, so it is mandatory there. Microsoft asks for a leading primary key element for split and merge. Salesforce uses it as the partition key on generic tables. The sources differ by implementation (C-16).
check_description: Primary keys of sharded tenant-scoped tables begin with the tenant identifier.

title: No per-tenant tables or columns
statement: A shared database SHOULD NOT create tables or columns for individual tenants, and tenant-specific fields SHOULD use a dedicated custom-data structure.
applies_when: Shared-database multi-tenant systems
rationale: Azure lists both as antipatterns, because schema drift grows with tenant count.
exceptions: Dedicated-database tenants under TEN-005.
engine_notes: none
check_description: No table or column name is specific to one tenant in a shared schema.

title: Tenant catalog and lifecycle
statement: Siloed, sharded and bridge deployments SHOULD maintain a tenant placement catalog and automate tenant onboarding, offboarding and restore.
applies_when: Siloed, sharded or bridge deployments
rationale: Hard-coded placement and manual tenant operations do not scale and risk acting on the wrong tenant.
exceptions: Fewer tenants than make automation worthwhile; approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: Schema version should be tracked per database in silo deployments (CLOUD-19). Offboarding retention follows the retention and erasure group's rules.
check_description: A catalog maps each tenant to its placement, and onboarding and restore runbooks are automated.

title: Analytical tenancy pattern
statement: An analytical platform MAY use multi-tenant tables, per-tenant objects or per-tenant accounts according to tenant count and isolation need.
applies_when: Multi-tenant analytical platforms. OLTP tenancy rules do not carry over automatically.
rationale: Per-account isolation does not reach large tenant counts, and shared tables rely on policy for separation.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: LAKE-13 (Snowflake) gives multi-tenant tables to millions, per-tenant objects to hundreds and per-tenant accounts to tens or low hundreds of tenants. Other platforms were not detailed. Streaming tenancy was not researched.
check_description: The analytical design records the chosen pattern and the tenant-count assumption.

title: Tenant and company are separate
statement: Multi-company SaaS systems SHOULD identify the tenant and the company separately, as the customer boundary and the legal and posting boundary respectively.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity and sold as multi-tenant SaaS
rationale: Treating one identifier as both cannot represent a customer with several legal entities. Company filtering is an authorization rule and does not replace tenant isolation.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Company-scoped tables carry the company identifier as well as the tenant identifier where the tenant scope applies.

title: Company identifier on ERP tables
statement: Transactional tables and most setup tables in an ERP SHOULD carry a company identifier.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity
rationale: ERP products use the company or legal entity as the posting boundary and sometimes the security boundary, and without the identifier neither can be applied.
exceptions: Master data intentionally shared across companies under TEN-022, and other tenant-shared setup tables approved by the data owner.
engine_notes: Dynamics 365 uses DataAreaId. SAP rests on training pages only.
check_description: Transactional and company-scoped setup tables carry the company identifier.

title: One company per posting
statement: A financial posting SHOULD be attributed to exactly one company.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity
rationale: Postings spanning companies cannot be balanced or reported per legal entity without decomposition.
exceptions: Intercompany transactions, handled under TEN-021. Decomposing them is a modeling choice, since NetSuite allows one transaction to post to two or more subsidiaries.
engine_notes: NetSuite generally posts a transaction to one subsidiary. Superseded by FIN-043 under OR-10.
check_description: Each posted line resolves to exactly one company.

title: Intercompany as linked balanced entries
statement: Intercompany transactions SHOULD be recorded as a linked pair of entries, each balanced per entity, with eliminations.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity
rationale: Unlinked entries cannot be reconciled or eliminated on consolidation.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: NetSuite posts to two or more subsidiaries; ERPNext balances each company's entry independently; Dynamics 365 uses directional legal-entity pairs; Oracle balances by legal entity. Superseded by FIN-047 under OR-11.
check_description: Each intercompany document links its entries, and each entity's side balances.

title: Master data scope
statement: An ERP MAY scope master data per company or share it across a tenant; the accepted default is tenant-shared master data with optional per-company restriction for each class.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity
rationale: Sources differ: Dynamics shared master data cannot be overridden per organization, while Odoo can restrict it by company. Both default to shared.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Each master data class has a recorded scope.

title: Company as access dimension
statement: An ERP MAY treat company as an access-control dimension where users are restricted by entity.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity with users restricted by entity
rationale: Without it, company-level restrictions depend on application convention. Cross-company roles such as group accountants need explicit modeling.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Dynamics 365 uses DataAreaId as a security boundary in some functional areas (TEN-08).
check_description: Role definitions state which companies each role can reach.

title: Consolidation hierarchy
statement: An ERP with consolidated reporting SHOULD model the company hierarchy as a tree with elimination entities.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity and statutory or consolidated reporting. The rule applies to the warehouse only where consolidation is run there.
rationale: Without a hierarchy, consolidation and elimination depend on off-system rework.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SAP rests on training pages only. Superseded by FIN-050 under OR-13.
check_description: A hierarchy exists with a root and elimination entities used for consolidated reports.

title: Legal entity, ledger and business unit are distinct
statement: An ERP SHOULD model legal entity, ledger and business unit as distinct concepts.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity
rationale: A single company concept cannot express entities that need several ledgers or units that cross entities.
exceptions: Single-entity systems with one ledger; approved by the finance owner.
engine_notes: Oracle separates balancing segment, ledger and business unit. Dynamics 365 configures a ledger per legal entity. No official SAP company-code definition was read. Superseded by FIN-042 under OR-14.
check_description: The conceptual model separates the three concepts or records why they are merged.

title: Consolidated statements under IFRS
statement: A system supporting a parent that presents consolidated statements under IFRS 10 MUST be able to produce the data for those statements.
applies_when: Parents presenting consolidated statements under IFRS 10, at concept level only. Matrix scope is consolidation.
rationale: The statements cannot be prepared without consolidated data. This rule requires legal review and accounting review of the applicable IFRS adoption.
exceptions: Entities outside IFRS 10 consolidation; determined by counsel and finance.
engine_notes: IFRS 10 was read as a summary page only, held as a supporting page under ERP-21. No paragraph is cited. Superseded by FIN-051 under OR-15.
check_description: Finance confirms consolidated statements can be produced from system data. Elimination paragraphs were not read and are not asserted.

title: Elimination location
statement: An ERP MAY hold intercompany eliminations in an elimination entity, at report time, at a posting level or by a line-level flag.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity and consolidation. Matrix scope is consolidation.
rationale: The choice trades traceability against reporting complexity.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Dynamics 365 uses an entity or report-time elimination; SAP uses posting level 20 (training pages only); NetSuite uses elimination journals. Superseded by FIN-048 under OR-16.
check_description: The design records where eliminations live.

title: Intercompany currency differences are expected
statement: Intercompany currency differences SHOULD be recorded to a defined account and not treated as errors.
applies_when: ERP or financial system holding more than one company or legal entity and multi-currency consolidation. Matrix scope is consolidation.
rationale: Treating expected differences as errors breaks reconciliation design.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: NetSuite uses CTA-E with its revaluation link. Dynamics 365 shows originating currency in elimination journals. Superseded by FIN-049 under OR-17.
check_description: Intercompany reconciliation books currency differences to the defined account.

title: Recovery objectives from BIA, NIST-governed systems
statement: NIST-governed systems MUST define RTO, RPO and MTD from a business impact analysis.
applies_when: US federal information systems, or systems bound to NIST SP 800-34 by regulation or contract
rationale: Without BIA-derived objectives, recovery design has no target. Requires legal review to confirm applicability for a given system.
exceptions: Requires legal review of applicability; none otherwise.
engine_notes: none
check_description: Confirm a current BIA exists and that RTO is shorter than MTD.

title: Recovery objectives from BIA, other systems
statement: Production systems outside NIST governance SHOULD define RTO, RPO and MTD from a business impact analysis.
applies_when: Production systems not covered by BDR-001
rationale: AWS and Google tie recovery design to stated objectives; assumed objectives surface only during an outage.
exceptions: Non-critical systems with a recorded owner acceptance of data loss.
engine_notes: ISO 22301:2019 is known to this research only through the EVS national record and is cited as such. The research notes label this MANDATORY for all production; the matrix holds it RECOMMENDED outside NIST-governed systems.
check_description: Confirm RTO, RPO and MTD are recorded per system with their BIA basis.

title: Point-in-time recovery foundation
statement: Systems requiring point-in-time recovery MUST take physical or snapshot-based base backups and continuously archive the transaction log.
applies_when: Point-in-time recovery is required by the system's RPO
rationale: Snapshots or dumps alone can recover only to the moment they were taken.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL: WAL level replica or higher; test archiving before the first base backup; archive commands must not overwrite and must report success correctly. MySQL: binary logging on, the 8.4 default. Oracle: ARCHIVELOG mode; backups taken in NOARCHIVELOG are unusable after switching ([WF] re-check against the page). SQL Server: full recovery with log backups. MongoDB: only Cloud and Ops Manager give point-in-time restore with guaranteed sharded consistency. Managed services differ; Cloud SQL point-in-time restore creates a new instance. That RPO is bounded by log archive frequency is inference.
check_description: Confirm base backups and log archiving are running without gaps, and that a recovery to a chosen time has succeeded.

title: Logical dumps supplement physical backups
statement: Logical dumps SHOULD be used only as a supplement to physical backups, for portability and partial restore.
applies_when: Physical backups are available for the engine
rationale: Logical dumps are not a point-in-time recovery solution, and Oracle states they are insufficient alone.
exceptions: Small MongoDB deployments, where mongodump is described as suitable; other small systems with the owner's recorded acceptance.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL pg_dump is the cross-version method and cannot be a PITR base. MySQL physical backups are faster but hardware-bound. File copies alone are not valid for InnoDB. Percona XtraBackup 8.0 reached end of life in June 2026.
check_description: Confirm the backup plan does not rely on logical dumps as its only recovery method.

title: Replicas are not backups
statement: Replicas and standbys MUST NOT be counted as a substitute for separate backups.
applies_when: The system's data is not reproducible from another source
rationale: Replication can carry corruption and malicious deletion to every copy.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL Server is the only database engine that states this explicitly; AWS states it for replication generally and says active-active still needs backups; Oracle Data Guard guidance offloads backups to a standby instead of replacing them. Matrix row BK-4 also cites OPS-20, but official_documentation.md section 16 finds that page concerns logical against physical backups, so it is omitted here.
check_description: Confirm every system with replicas also has independent backups.

title: Table history is not backup
statement: Time travel, table history and platform-internal recovery features MUST NOT be the only recovery mechanism for warehouse or lakehouse data that must be recoverable beyond the feature's retention window.
applies_when: The data is not reproducible from sources within the system's RTO
rationale: These windows are bounded and some features are not accessible to customers.
exceptions: Data fully reproducible from retained sources, recorded by the data owner.
engine_notes: Databricks says not to use table history for long-term archival, and raising retention raises storage cost. Snowflake Fail-safe is for Snowflake's use only and not an access path to history; Time Travel retention is bounded.
check_description: Confirm a separate backup or reproducibility record exists for each dataset needing recovery beyond the window.

title: Restores are tested and verified
statement: Every backup strategy MUST include scheduled restore tests whose results are verified for consistency.
applies_when: always, for systems of record and for warehouse or lakehouse data not reproducible from sources
rationale: A backup that has not been restored is unproven, and GitLab's January 31 outage postmortem showed backups can be unusable when they are needed.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL Server: restore to a test system and check consistency. The test frequency is not set by any source read and is left to each system's RTO and RPO. OPS-22 was read earlier and was bot-blocked at the 2026-11-08 link check.
check_description: Report the date and result of the latest verified restore per system and alert when one is overdue.

title: Restore tests cover the application stack
statement: Restoration tests SHOULD cover the whole application stack and be judged on integrity, RTO and RPO.
applies_when: The application depends on more than one data store or service
rationale: A database that restores cleanly can still leave the application unusable.
exceptions: Systems with no dependent application.
engine_notes: Stated by Google only; official_documentation.md section 15 records it as not yet a general rule. AWS requires failover testing, which is a different activity.
evidence: research/official_documentation.md#Restoration tests covering the whole application stack
check_description: Confirm restore test reports include application-level checks and integrity, RTO and RPO results.

title: Recovery rehearsed and timed
statement: Full recovery SHOULD be rehearsed regularly and its duration measured against RTO.
applies_when: The system has a stated RTO
rationale: GitHub found large cluster restores slow and not fully rehearsed; an unmeasured RTO is an assumption.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: data_engineering_principles.md DR-03 reports that AWS and Azure advise periodic testing, but official_documentation.md section 16 narrows the cloud claims on restore testing, so neither is relied on here. The research notes label rehearsal MANDATORY for all production; the matrix holds it as RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Report measured recovery duration from the latest rehearsal against RTO.

title: Backup schedule meets RPO
statement: Backup and log archive schedules SHOULD be set to meet the system's RPO.
applies_when: The system has a stated RPO
rationale: A schedule set by habit can miss the data-loss limit the business has accepted.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Stated by Google; AWS ties strategy to objectives. AWS tier ranges are in a figure and were not captured, so no numbers are given.
check_description: Compare the actual interval between backups or archived logs with the RPO.

title: Named owner for restore capability
statement: Each system SHOULD have a named owner for its backup and restore capability.
applies_when: always
rationale: GitLab's backup failure was attributed to lack of ownership.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: none
check_description: Confirm each system records an owner for restore capability.

title: 3-2-1 baseline with an offline copy
statement: Backups SHOULD follow the 3-2-1 baseline and SHOULD keep an offline, encrypted copy that is tested regularly.
applies_when: Systems of record with ransomware exposure
rationale: Ransomware variants try to find and delete or encrypt accessible backups.
exceptions: Offline copy may be replaced by an approved immutable copy under BDR-013; approved by the security owner.
engine_notes: 3-2-1 comes from CISA Data Backup Options, not from OPS-22. OPS-22 is the source for offline, encrypted copies. The research notes label the offline copy MANDATORY; the matrix holds this row as RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Confirm copy count, media or location separation, and the last test of the offline copy.

title: Immutable backup copy
statement: Systems MAY hold an immutable backup copy in addition to the baseline; the accepted default is one immutable copy for systems of record, with compliance and misconfiguration reviewed.
applies_when: Ransomware exposure is in scope
rationale: Immutability resists deletion, but the only strong promotion is vendor marketing and CISA adds cautions on compliance and misconfiguration (conflict C12), so the default is a judgment.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Veeam's 3-2-1-1-0 extension is vendor marketing. Azure SQL guidance mentions backup immutability. Check erasure handling under RET-026, which stays provisional.
check_description: Confirm that any immutable copy has a reviewed retention setting and that its legal effect has been considered.

title: Backups encrypted, separated, least privilege
statement: Backups SHOULD be encrypted, stored separately from primary systems, and accessible only with least privilege.
applies_when: always
rationale: Backups held beside the primary fail with it and expose the same data if compromised.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Separate accounts or regions protect against compromise (AWS). Managed services differ on what survives deletion of the instance, so confirm per service. The research notes label this MANDATORY; the matrix holds it as RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Confirm encryption, separate storage location and access lists for backups.

title: Backup keys recoverable
statement: Keys or certificates needed to decrypt backups SHOULD be stored separately from the backups and be available during recovery.
applies_when: Backups or the database are encrypted
rationale: Encrypted backups are unrecoverable without their keys.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQL Server states that certificates must be backed up when TDE is used. The matrix has no separate row; this follows the level of BK-8.
check_description: Confirm key location, separation from backups, and inclusion of keys in restore tests.

title: DR tier chosen from BIA
statement: Each system MAY select a disaster recovery tier from backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby or active/active, based on its RTO, RPO and cost.
applies_when: A BIA exists under BDR-001 or BDR-002
rationale: Choosing a tier without the objectives either overspends or misses them.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: AWS names four tiers; NIST names cold, warm, hot, mobile and mirrored sites. RPO and RTO figures per tier were not captured, so none are stated. On Azure SQL, geo-restore is the most basic option and failover groups are advised for business-critical applications.
check_description: Confirm the chosen tier is recorded and traced to the objectives.

title: Failover topology constraints encoded
statement: OLTP failover automation SHOULD encode topology constraints that prevent divergent writes.
applies_when: Automated failover is in use across sites or regions
rationale: Divergent writes were the costliest failure in GitHub's 2018 incident.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Evidence is one operator's MySQL topology.
check_description: Confirm failover automation documents which promotions it refuses, and that this was tested.

title: Per-tenant restore approach
statement: Multi-tenant systems MAY provide per-tenant restore through tenant-isolated databases or selective recovery from a side copy.
applies_when: The tenancy model or contracts call for restoring a single tenant
rationale: In a shared pool, restoring one tenant by rolling back the whole database harms all others.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Silo databases restore in place; pool models need selective recovery. Evidence is Azure guidance. No source quantifies effort.
check_description: Confirm the tenant restore method is documented and has been tested for a sample tenant.

title: Verify state after recovery
statement: After recovery, the database SHOULD be inspected to confirm it reached the desired state before service resumes.
applies_when: Any recovery event or rehearsal
rationale: A recovery that stopped at the wrong point can return bad data to service.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL advises verifying the desired state. Reconciling derived stores against the restored source is inference.
check_description: Confirm the recovery runbook has a state-check step and a record of its result.

title: Pipeline state in DR planning
statement: DR plans for systems with change data capture SHOULD include replication slots and connector offsets.
applies_when: Change data capture reads from the recovered database
rationale: Slots and offsets are bound to a database's history, so a recovery or failover can lose or repeat changes.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Debezium warns that dropping a slot on the primary loses data. The DR scope is inference, and no source read covers re-establishing CDC after failover. The research notes label this MANDATORY; an inference-only rule cannot be MANDATORY.
check_description: Confirm the DR plan lists CDC slots and offsets and the steps to re-establish them.

title: CDC re-established after failover
statement: After a database failover or restore, change data capture SHOULD be re-established by a documented procedure that confirms each replication slot and connector offset matches the recovered database before consumers resume.
applies_when: Change data capture reads from a database that has failed over or been restored
rationale: Slots and offsets bind to one database history, so resuming capture without checking them can lose or repeat changes. No source read covers re-establishing CDC after failover; this is an inference.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Inference only, from Debezium's warning that dropping a slot on the primary loses data and from DR-06. No engine procedure was researched. BDR-020 puts slots and offsets in the DR plan; this rule covers the recovery step.
check_description: Confirm the recovery procedure has this step, and that a rehearsal shows consumers resume without loss or duplication.

title: Versioned, tool-applied schema changes
statement: Every schema change to a permanent environment SHOULD be a versioned script held in version control and applied by a migration tool that records what was applied.
applies_when: always; for warehouse and lakehouse platforms, where DDL is managed through migrations or versioned models
rationale: Manual changes leave environments out of step and cannot be reproduced or audited; Azure lists manual schema change as an antipattern.
exceptions: Emergency manual change during an incident, recorded and back-ported to version control afterward; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: Flyway, Liquibase, Alembic, Prisma and Atlas keep a history record in different forms. Warehouse teams may use versioned model code in place of migration scripts.
check_description: Confirm each environment has a migration history and that every applied entry matches a script in version control.

title: Applied migrations are immutable
statement: A migration already applied to a permanent environment SHOULD NOT be edited; corrections SHOULD be made by a new migration.
applies_when: Migration-based or hybrid authoring is in use
rationale: Editing an applied migration makes environments diverge silently and invalidates the recorded history.
exceptions: Comment-only or formatting repair using the tool's documented repair command; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: Flyway checksums detect edits to applied versioned migrations. Rails guidance gives the same direction.
check_description: Compare stored checksums or file hashes of applied migrations with the repository and fail on any change.

title: Authoring model chosen and recorded
statement: Each system MAY use state-based, migration-based or hybrid authoring, and SHOULD record the choice; the accepted default is hybrid with the planned migration checked in.
applies_when: always
rationale: State-based tools can lose data on renames and pure migration histories accumulate; sources agree neither is ideal and no benchmark settles it, so the default is a judgment.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Atlas and Prisma derive a migration from desired state and check in the plan. Legacy Prisma Migrate behaviour was not verified against ORM 8 documentation.
check_description: Confirm the system's design record names its authoring model and that any generated plan is committed before it is applied.

title: Expand and contract for incompatible change
statement: On live OLTP systems, each schema change SHOULD be deployable while the previous application version runs, and incompatible changes SHOULD use expand, migrate and contract across separate releases.
applies_when: The system is deployed while serving traffic; covers renames, type changes and drops of columns or tables
rationale: A change that breaks the running application version causes an outage even when the DDL itself takes no long lock, which is why a drop can be lock-safe and still application-unsafe (conflict C2).
exceptions: Systems with an agreed maintenance window that stops all application versions; approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: Dropping a column is catalog-only on PostgreSQL but still breaks ORM caches; GitLab spreads it over three releases. Support for at least one prior schema version is stated by Azure only and is not a general rule. The every-change-deployable wording is the research authors' meta-rule [INFERENCE].
check_description: For each rename, type change or drop, confirm the release plan shows the expand, migrate and contract steps in separate releases.

title: Rollback stance
statement: OLTP migrations SHOULD be forward-only and rely on backward compatibility and tested backups for recovery, with down scripts optional and tested.
applies_when: always on OLTP systems
rationale: Down scripts cover only some change types and cannot restore dropped data, so relying on them gives false assurance; sources disagree on whether reversibility is required (conflict C1).
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: GitLab requires reversibility with exceptions; Braintree does not revert schema to roll back; Flyway undo is limited and points to backward compatibility; Liquibase treats rollback as first-class with limits and no automatic rollback for drops, raw SQL or data operations; Prisma has no down files.
check_description: Confirm the migration policy states the rollback stance and that each release plan names its recovery route.

title: Developer authored, DBA reviewed
statement: Schema migrations SHOULD be authored by the delivery team, checked by automation and reviewed by the people responsible for the production database.
applies_when: always
rationale: Adopting migration practice without the production database owners meets resistance and bypasses their knowledge of production behaviour.
exceptions: DBA-authored migrations are acceptable where the team has no developer ownership of the schema; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: none. No source quantifies developer-authored against DBA-authored outcomes.
check_description: Confirm each merged migration has a review from a named production database owner.

title: Generated migrations are candidates
statement: Tool-generated migrations SHOULD be reviewed and corrected before merge and SHOULD NOT be applied unchanged.
applies_when: A tool or ORM generates the migration
rationale: Generators cannot detect renames and report them as a drop and an add, which loses data if applied as produced.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Alembic states that manual review is always necessary. Topic note 13 labelled this MANDATORY; the matrix holds it as RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Confirm generated migrations show review, and that any drop-plus-add pair was checked for being a rename.

title: Separate lock and runtime budgets
statement: Migrations on live OLTP systems SHOULD state separate budgets for lock hold time and total runtime, set per system from rehearsal, and SHOULD fail or be replanned when rehearsal exceeds them; no value set framework-wide.
applies_when: Migrations run against tables serving live traffic
rationale: Lock hold and runtime are different quantities, and an unbounded one stalls application traffic. The quoted operator values measure different things and no independent benchmark exists, so any default is a judgment.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Operator values, not portable defaults: Braintree about 2 seconds exclusive lock hold; strong_migrations 10 second lock timeout example; GitLab 15 second statement timeout, and 3, 10 and 20 minute limits by migration type. A statement timeout is not a lock-hold limit. Braintree covers PostgreSQL 9.1 to 12, so re-check against current versions.
check_description: Confirm both budgets are stated and compare rehearsal lock and duration measurements against them.

title: Bounded lock acquisition
statement: Migrations on live OLTP systems SHOULD acquire locks with a short timeout and retry, after checking for long-running queries.
applies_when: Migrations run against tables serving live traffic
rationale: A waiting lock request queues all later queries on the table, so a blocked migration can stall traffic before it has acquired anything.
exceptions: Dedicated maintenance windows with no traffic; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: The queueing behaviour is documented for PostgreSQL. Timeout mechanisms differ by engine. The research notes label this MANDATORY; the matrix states nothing in this area is MANDATORY.
check_description: Confirm each migration touching an existing table sets a lock timeout and has a defined retry.

title: Use non-blocking DDL paths on large tables
statement: DDL on large or high-traffic OLTP tables SHOULD use the engine's documented online or staged path rather than a blocking form where such a path exists.
applies_when: The table is large or high-traffic; thresholds are set per system
rationale: Blocking index builds, constraint validation and table rewrites stop writes, and sometimes reads, for the length of the operation.
exceptions: Small tables, new empty tables, and operations with no documented online path, such as PostgreSQL exclusion constraints; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: PostgreSQL: concurrent index builds outside a transaction, constraints added unvalidated and validated later, batched backfill. MySQL: INSTANT or INPLACE where available, otherwise an online tool. [WF] The MySQL 8.4 online DDL matrix was read through a summarising tool only; re-check against the manual before use. Safe sequences per operation are in data_engineering_principles.md section 3.3 and depend on engine version.
check_description: Flag blocking forms of index, constraint and type-change operations on tables above the system's size threshold, allowing recorded waivers.

title: Online change tool selected deliberately
statement: Where an external online schema change tool is needed, the system MAY use a trigger-based or log-based tool and SHOULD record why; the accepted default is log-based unless constraints rule it out.
applies_when: MySQL-family engines on tables where native online DDL is unsuitable
rationale: Each mechanism has limits and each project describes itself favorably; no independent comparison exists, so the default is a judgment.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: pt-online-schema-change uses triggers and will not run on tables that already have triggers. gh-ost reads the binlog and treats triggers as a source of risk. Test on a replica and verify backups first. Managed platforms may provide their own ghost-table workflow.
check_description: Confirm the migration plan names the tool and the reason, and that the table meets the tool's documented conditions.

title: Large backfills batched outside DDL
statement: Large data backfills SHOULD run batched and throttled outside the DDL transaction.
applies_when: The backfill volume can hold locks or load beyond the system's budgets
rationale: A backfill inside the DDL transaction holds its locks for the entire backfill.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: GitLab uses batched background migrations. Stripe ran its large backfills offline.
check_description: Flag data modification statements inside a migration that also performs DDL, and confirm large backfills have batch size and throttle settings.

title: Placement of small data changes
statement: Small data changes SHOULD be separate from schema changes, as a reviewed data migration in the same versioned history.
applies_when: A data change accompanies a schema change and is too small to need a batched backfill
rationale: Mixing data and schema changes complicates review and lock behaviour; sources disagree on where data changes belong (conflict C4), and the threshold is volume-dependent.
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Rails discourages data changes in migrations; GitLab allows post-deployment and batched ones; Django provides a data migration step.
check_description: Confirm that data changes follow the approved placement and are reviewed like schema changes.

title: Transaction boundary for DDL
statement: On high-traffic OLTP systems, each DDL statement SHOULD run in its own transaction, and other systems SHOULD use one transaction per migration where the engine supports it.
applies_when: The engine supports transactional DDL
rationale: One transaction per migration gives atomicity but holds several objects' locks at once, and sources disagree (conflict C3).
exceptions: Deviation from the accepted default needs a recorded reason approved by the framework exception approver.
engine_notes: Django and Flyway wrap migrations in a transaction by default where supported; Braintree does not combine DDL statements. When removing foreign keys use a consistent lock order. Concurrent index builds cannot run in a transaction on PostgreSQL.
check_description: Flag migrations that put several DDL statements in one transaction on systems marked high-traffic.

title: Safety rules tied to engine version
statement: Each migration safety rule SHOULD state the engine and version range it applies to.
applies_when: always
rationale: Rules go stale when defaults change; adding a column with a constant default was unsafe before PostgreSQL 11 and is metadata-only afterward (conflict C5).
exceptions: none
engine_notes: PostgreSQL rewrite behaviour changed over versions. CASE-27 is 2014-era and must be re-checked against current versions before use.
check_description: Confirm each engine-specific migration rule or lint configuration records its version range.

title: Verify large data migrations
statement: Large OLTP data migrations SHOULD verify the new path against the old, for example through dual writes and comparison reads, before switching reads.
applies_when: A data model or storage migration moves live data
rationale: Without comparison, defects in the new path surface only after the old path is gone.
exceptions: Small migrations verified by reconciliation counts; approved by the system owner.
engine_notes: Stripe used a comparison harness on hundreds of millions of objects. This rule also covers matrix row TS-11, so no separate TST rule exists. All sources are single-operator reports.
check_description: Confirm the migration plan names a comparison method and that mismatch results were reviewed before cutover.

title: Portable safe changes on table formats
statement: Lakehouse tables intended to stay portable across table formats SHOULD limit in-place schema evolution to the changes all target formats support: adding a nullable column, widening integer and float types, and widening decimal types.
applies_when: Tables are or may be read through more than one table format
rationale: A change safe in one format can break readers on another.
exceptions: Single-format tables may use that format's wider evolution rules; approved by the data platform owner.
engine_notes: Iceberg, Delta and Hudi differ beyond this set. The Hudi promotion matrix was reconstructed from flattened page text and should be verified on the page. OLTP migration rules do not apply here.
check_description: Compare the proposed schema change against the supported set for every format that reads the table.

title: Breaking changes in event streams
statement: Event schemas SHOULD evolve compatibly, and a change that compatibility cannot express SHOULD use a dual upgrade with a versioned topic.
applies_when: Schemas are shared between producers and consumers on a stream
rationale: An incompatible change breaks consumers still reading the earlier form.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Confluent Schema Registry compatibility modes are the evidenced mechanism; other registries were not assessed here.
check_description: Run the registry's compatibility check against the proposed schema and confirm that breaking changes have a versioned topic and consumer migration plan.

title: Breaking changes to contracted models
statement: Removal, type change or constraint removal on a contracted analytical model SHOULD be classified as breaking and released under a new model version.
applies_when: The model has a published contract or external consumers
rationale: A silent contract change breaks downstream consumers.
exceptions: Internal models with no consumers outside the owning team.
engine_notes: dbt model contracts and versions are the evidenced mechanism. dbt warns that adopting model versions too early raises maintenance cost. DQ-03 and LAKE-17 are the same page, so this is single-vendor evidence. The research notes label this MANDATORY; the matrix holds it as RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Diff the proposed contract against the published one and fail on breaking changes with no new version.

title: Per-tenant schema version tracking
statement: Systems using one database or schema per tenant MAY track the applied schema version per tenant.
applies_when: Tenants are isolated into separate databases or schemas
rationale: Without per-tenant version records, partial rollouts leave tenants on unknown versions.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Stated by Azure only; recorded in official_documentation.md section 15 as not yet a general rule.
check_description: Confirm each tenant has a recorded schema version and report tenants behind the current one.

title: Three-tier schema change gate
statement: Schema changes SHOULD pass static lint, then a real-engine apply with tests, then a production-like rehearsal before production.
applies_when: always; the rehearsal tier applies where a production-like dataset can be provided
rationale: Each tier catches failures the others miss, and skipping one lets those failures reach production. The three-tier shape is the research authors' synthesis of the tool set.
exceptions: A tier may be skipped with a recorded waiver from the database owner.
engine_notes: The tool for each tier varies by engine; see TST-002, TST-003 and TST-004.
check_description: Confirm the delivery pipeline runs all three tiers in order and blocks promotion on failure.

title: Static migration lint with waivers
statement: OLTP migrations SHOULD pass a static lint for blocking and destructive patterns, with explicit recorded waivers for intended exceptions.
applies_when: A linter exists for the engine in use
rationale: Blocking and destructive DDL is easy to miss in review; lint stops it before it runs.
exceptions: Waiver per rule and migration, approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: Existing tools cover this: Squawk (PostgreSQL), Atlas, Liquibase policy checks, strong_migrations. Atlas and Liquibase rule engines are paid. Squawk's required-field rule concerns migration safety and is not a table policy. SQLFluff is a style linter and not a safety tool.
check_description: Existing tool coverage. Run the linter on every migration; failures block merge unless a waiver is recorded.

title: Schema assertions in tests
statement: OLTP schemas SHOULD have automated assertions on structure and behaviour of critical objects, run in the delivery pipeline.
applies_when: A test framework exists for the engine in use
rationale: Linters do not confirm that the deployed schema behaves as designed, and constraints go untested otherwise.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Existing tools: pgTAP, tSQLt, utPLSQL; assertions are written per object, so a schema-wide sweep needs generated tests. tSQLt warns that a faked table does not test its constraints.
check_description: Existing tool coverage. Confirm assertions run for critical objects and that constraint tests are not run against faked tables.

title: Test on a real engine
statement: OLTP migration and schema tests SHOULD run on a disposable instance of the same engine and version as production rather than on a mock.
applies_when: The engine can be provisioned for testing
rationale: Engine semantics differ by version, so mocks and other engines miss real failures.
exceptions: Managed engines with no disposable equivalent may use a shared test instance; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: Testcontainers supplies throwaway engines and performs no checks itself; it must be paired with the tools in TST-002 and TST-003.
check_description: Confirm the pipeline's test engine and version match production.

title: Production-like rehearsal
statement: OLTP schema changes SHOULD be rehearsed against a production-like dataset, with sensitive data masked or synthetic, and with timing compared to thresholds.
applies_when: A production-like dataset can be provided within data protection rules
rationale: Lock duration and backfill time depend on data volume and distribution, which small fixtures hide.
exceptions: Masking requirements are set by security rule SC-12, which is MANDATORY under PCI and US federal scope; those requirements are not waivable here.
engine_notes: GitLab uses thin clones of production for this check. DORA's test-every-change wording is confirmed in note 22.
check_description: Confirm the rehearsal uses masked or synthetic production-like data, and record duration and lock measurements against thresholds.

title: Schema drift detection
statement: Deployed schemas SHOULD be compared continuously or on a schedule with the version-controlled intended state, and differences SHOULD raise an alert.
applies_when: always on OLTP systems; extend to warehouses where DDL is version controlled
rationale: Out-of-band changes invalidate tests and can break later migrations.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Existing tools: Atlas drift detection; Flyway checksums guard edits to applied migrations; Prisma stops on out-of-band change; PlanetScale rejects direct DDL. EF Core's HasPendingModelChanges can back a test for a missing migration. Scope includes data_warehouse to match applies_when; matrix row TS-6 is scoped OLTP.
check_description: Existing tool coverage. Compare the live catalog with intended state and report any differences.

title: Custom checks for framework policies
statement: Framework policies that existing tools do not check, including tenant keys, money types and audit columns, SHOULD have custom automated validators.
applies_when: The schema is subject to these policies
rationale: Without a validator these policies rely on review alone; no tool read ships a named rule for tenant keys, money types or audit columns.
exceptions: A check may be replaced by a documented assertion suite for the affected tables; approved by the database owner.
engine_notes: Not-found marks in the research mean not found in the pages read and are not proof of absence. Paid rule engines (Atlas Pro, Liquibase Secure) offer custom rules. See the tool coverage table in the rules file.
check_description: Stage 3 custom validators required for tenant keys (TST-016), money types (TST-015) and audit columns (TST-017). Confirm each is implemented or waived.

title: Analytical model tests
statement: Warehouse and lakehouse models SHOULD have unique and not-null tests on their primary key, relationship tests where relevant, and unit tests for non-trivial logic.
applies_when: Models are built by a transformation or orchestration tool
rationale: Most analytical platforms do not enforce declared keys, so tests are the available check on them.
exceptions: Models without a defined grain, recorded in the model documentation.
engine_notes: dbt data tests and unit tests; Dagster asset checks. OLTP test tooling does not apply.
check_description: Existing tool coverage. Confirm each model has key tests and that failures are reported or block as the dataset's tier requires.

title: Test rollback paths that exist
statement: Where down scripts exist, they SHOULD be tested by deploy, rollback and redeploy.
applies_when: The migration has a down script
rationale: Complex structural and data changes are hard to roll back, and an untested rollback may fail when it is needed.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Liquibase documents deploy, rollback and redeploy testing, with automatic rollback limited to certain change types. Depends on the outcome of MIG-005.
check_description: Confirm the pipeline applies, reverts and re-applies migrations that declare a down path.

title: Concurrency anomaly testing
statement: Teams MAY run isolation anomaly tests per engine and version for correctness-critical transaction flows.
applies_when: Correctness depends on a specific isolation guarantee
rationale: Engines differ in what each isolation level prevents, and assumptions can be wrong.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Hermitage or Jepsen style reassessment. Jepsen tested MySQL 8.0.34, so re-check against 8.4 before relying on it. Hermitage does not state engine versions.
check_description: Confirm any such test records the engine, version and isolation level tested.

title: Automated change delivery
statement: All production schema changes SHOULD be delivered through an automated pipeline.
applies_when: always
rationale: Manual delivery bypasses the gates in TST-001.
exceptions: Incident changes under MIG-001's exception.
engine_notes: DORA presents 100 percent automation as a capability goal; the research notes label this MANDATORY but the matrix holds it as RECOMMENDED.
check_description: Compare production migration history with pipeline runs and report changes with no pipeline record.

title: Foreign key index check
statement: Where the framework's indexing rule requires an index on a foreign key, the requirement SHOULD be checked automatically.
applies_when: The indexing standard (matrix row IX-3) requires an index for the engine and ownership case
rationale: A missing index is invisible until load exposes it. Whether one is needed depends on the engine and who creates it.
exceptions: As set by the indexing standard.
engine_notes: Existing tools cover this: Schemalint index-referencing-column and prisma-lint require-field-index are built in; Atlas has a Pro custom rule; pgTAP asserts per object. EF Core creates the index by convention. GitLab requires it only inside GitLab. Squawk's foreign key rule concerns locks and does not check indexes.
check_description: Existing tool coverage. Report foreign keys lacking a supporting index where the indexing standard requires one.

title: Primary key and required-column check
statement: Primary key presence and framework-required columns SHOULD be checked automatically.
applies_when: The schema is subject to these policies
rationale: A table without a primary key or a required column passes review easily and is costly to fix later.
exceptions: As set by the integrity and audit standards.
engine_notes: Existing tools cover this: Schemalint and prisma-lint built in; Atlas custom (Pro); pgTAP assertions. prisma-lint reads schema files and Schemalint reads a live catalog. Liquibase built-in check lists returned 404, so they are not cited.
check_description: Existing tool coverage. Report tables lacking a primary key or a framework-required column.

title: Reserved word check
statement: Identifiers MAY be checked against reserved words for the target engine, beyond what the engine itself rejects.
applies_when: Identifiers may move between engines or dialects
rationale: A word reserved in another dialect can break a later port, and existing tool coverage is thin.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: SQLFluff RF04 is the only linter rule found; it is partial and dialect-dependent and excludes reserved keywords from its own scope. A full check needs a custom Stage 3 validator using each engine's reserved word list.
check_description: Partial tool coverage; Stage 3 custom validator needed for full coverage. Compare identifiers with reserved word lists for each target engine.

title: Money type check
statement: Columns holding money SHOULD be checked automatically against the framework's approved money types.
applies_when: The schema holds monetary values and the data types standard defines the approved types
rationale: Inexact money columns cause rounding errors that review can miss; no built-in money rule was found in any tool read.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Generic routes only: pgTAP col_type_is per column, tSQLt schema comparison, prisma-lint require-field-type by field name. Identifying which columns hold money needs a framework convention or metadata. The class is the matrix's and applies to the checking mechanism; the money-type requirement belongs to the data types standard. Level raised from OPTIONAL to RECOMMENDED by owner decision A18, a recorded departure from the matrix; evidence_strength is unchanged.
check_description: Stage 3 custom validator required, built as an engine-neutral catalog query. Identify money columns from metadata or convention and report any column not using an approved type.

title: Tenant key check
statement: Tenant-scoped tables SHOULD be checked automatically for the framework's tenant key.
applies_when: The system is multi-tenant in a shared schema or database
rationale: A missing tenant column can expose one tenant's data to another; no tool read ships a rule named for tenant keys.
exceptions: Tables marked as shared or global by the tenancy standard.
engine_notes: Generic routes only: Schemalint mandatory-columns, prisma-lint require-field (its documentation uses tenantId as an example), Atlas predicates (Pro), pgTAP has_column. Schemalint row-level-security and Atlas ensure-row-security-enabled check row-level security, which is a different check. The class applies to the checking mechanism; the tenant key requirement belongs to the tenancy standard. Level raised from OPTIONAL to RECOMMENDED by owner decision A18, a recorded departure from the matrix; evidence_strength is unchanged.
check_description: Stage 3 custom validator required, built as an engine-neutral catalog query. Report tenant-scoped tables lacking the tenant key, excluding approved global tables.

title: Audit column check
statement: Tables subject to the audit standard SHOULD be checked automatically for the framework's required audit columns.
applies_when: The audit standard requires audit columns on the table
rationale: A missing audit column loses history that cannot be recovered later; no tool read has a rule named for audit columns.
exceptions: As set by the audit standard.
engine_notes: Required-column rules are the available mechanism; this use is inference from the research, with no document showing it. The matrix has no row for this check; the level matches the sibling rows TS-16 and TS-17. Level raised from OPTIONAL to RECOMMENDED by owner decision A18, a recorded departure from the matrix; evidence_strength is unchanged.
check_description: Stage 3 custom validator required, built as an engine-neutral catalog query. Report tables in audit scope lacking a required audit column.

title: Layered validation
statement: Validation SHOULD combine source constraints, pipeline gates and warehouse tests according to the failure class each catches.
applies_when: always
rationale: Each layer catches a different failure class, so relying on one leaves the others undetected.
exceptions: Exception recorded with a reason and approved by the dataset owner
engine_notes: No controlled comparison of defect-catch rates exists, so the layering is a judgment.
check_description: The dataset's validation plan names the layer covering each failure class.

title: OLTP constraints at the source
statement: OLTP systems of record MUST enforce integrity with database constraints at the point of write.
applies_when: the system is a non-sharded OLTP system of record; this rule does not apply to analytical systems
rationale: Nothing downstream can retroactively enforce what the source admitted.
exceptions: Exception recorded with a reason and approved by the framework exception approver
engine_notes: Detailed constraint rules belong to the relational integrity standards. Where foreign keys are unavailable, RI-2 keeps FK columns, indexes, orphan audits and a documented risk.
check_description: Tables in the system of record declare their key, reference and value constraints.

title: Declared keys are not assumed enforced
statement: Analytical platforms MUST NOT rely on a declared primary key, foreign key or unique constraint as proof of integrity unless the platform documents enforcement for that table type.
applies_when: always, on warehouse and lakehouse tables; this is the opposite of the OLTP position in DQA-002
rationale: Standard warehouses accept duplicates and orphans silently, and a declaration suggests a guarantee that does not exist.
exceptions: none
engine_notes: Snowflake standard tables and Databricks do not enforce PK, FK or UNIQUE; NOT NULL and CHECK are enforced. Snowflake hybrid tables enforce them. Microsoft Fabric records them only. Platform documentation prevails over dbt's summary.
check_description: For each analytical table type in use, the record states which constraints the platform enforces.

title: Substitute for key uniqueness
statement: Every analytical model SHOULD have uniqueness and non-null tests on its key, plus pipeline merge on that key, in place of enforced keys.
applies_when: the platform does not enforce the key for this table type (DQA-003)
rationale: Without a substitute, duplicates inflate measures with no error raised.
exceptions: Exception recorded with a reason and approved by the dataset owner
engine_notes: dbt recommends the primary-key test. Tests run after the data exists, so publishing depends on DQA-007 and DQA-008.
check_description: Each model has passing unique and not-null tests on its declared key.

title: Substitute for referential integrity
statement: Foreign key relationships in analytical models SHOULD be protected by relationship tests or ETL key lookups with an orphan count.
applies_when: the platform does not enforce foreign keys for this table type (DQA-003)
rationale: Orphans silently drop rows in inner joins, and no error is raised.
exceptions: Exception recorded with a reason and approved by the dataset owner
engine_notes: Kimball-method fact tables pair lookups with default dimension rows (RPT-006).
check_description: Relationship tests or lookup orphan counts exist for each declared foreign key.

title: Trust-the-constraint settings
